sentences.zh: 李標，字汝立，高邑人。

translations.literal: Li Biao, styled Ruli, was a man of Gaoyi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Biao, whose style was Ruli, came from Gaoyi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年進士。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fifth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-fifth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a bachelor and appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: He was made a Hanlin bachelor and then appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 泰昌時，累遷少詹事。

translations.literal: In the Taichang reign he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taichang reign he rose step by step to Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，擢拜禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently directed the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he was elevated to Right Vice Minister of Rites and put in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 標師同邑越南星，黨人忌之，列名《東林同誌錄》中。

translations.literal: Biao's teacher was Yue Nanxing of the same district; partisan foes envied him and listed his name in the Record of Donglin Comrades.
translations.idiomatic: Biao had studied under Yue Nanxing, a fellow townsman; enemies in the factions resented this and entered his name in the Record of Donglin Comrades.

sentences.zh: 標懼禍，引疾歸。

translations.literal: Biao feared disaster and cited illness to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing reprisals, Biao pleaded illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝嗣位，即家拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor succeeded, Biao was appointed from home as Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor took the throne, Biao was summoned from retirement as Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年三月入朝。

translations.literal: In the third month of the first year of Chongzhen he entered court.
translations.idiomatic: He came to court in the third month of Chongzhen 1.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李國𣚴、來宗道、楊景辰相繼去，標遂為首輔。

translations.literal: Before long Li Guogan, Lai Zongdao, and Yang Jingchen left office in succession, and Biao then became chief grand secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Li Guogan, Lai Zongdao, and Yang Jingchen had all left office in turn, and Biao became chief grand secretary.

sentences.zh: 帝銳意圖治，恒召大臣面決庶政。

translations.literal: The emperor was keen to govern well and constantly summoned ministers to decide routine affairs face to face.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was determined to set things right and often called ministers before him to settle routine business on the spot.

sentences.zh: 宣府巡撫李養沖疏言旗尉往來如織，蹤跡難憑，且慮費無所出。

translations.literal: The Xuanfu grand coordinator Li Yangchong memorialized that banner guards came and went thick as weaving, their tracks hard to verify, and that he feared expenses with no source.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yangchong, grand coordinator of Xuanfu, reported that banner guards swarmed back and forth like woven cloth, their movements impossible to track, and that the cost had nowhere to come from.

sentences.zh: 帝以示標等曰：「邊情危急，遣旗尉偵探，奈何以為偽？

translations.literal: The emperor showed it to Biao and the others, saying: "The border situation is critical; we send banner guards to spy—how can this be called false?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor showed the memorial to Biao and his colleagues and said, "The frontier is in crisis—we send banner guards to scout. How can you call that false?

sentences.zh: 且祖宗朝設立廠衛，奚為者？

translations.literal: Moreover, why did the ancestral court establish the factory guards?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, why did our forefathers set up the factory guards in the first place?

sentences.zh: 」標對曰：「事固宜慎。

translations.literal: " Biao replied: "The matter should indeed be handled with care.
translations.idiomatic: " Biao answered, "The matter certainly calls for caution.

sentences.zh: 養沖以為不賂恐毀言日至，賂之則物力難勝耳。

translations.literal: Yangchong thinks that without bribes slander will come daily, yet if bribed the material burden cannot be borne."
translations.idiomatic: What Yangchong means is that without bribes he will face slander every day, but if he bribes them the treasury cannot bear the strain."

sentences.zh: 」帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said nothing.

sentences.zh: 同官劉鴻訓以增敕事為御史吳玉所糾，帝欲置鴻訓於法，標力辯其納賄之誣。

translations.literal: His colleague Liu Hongxun was impeached by Censor Wu Yu over augmenting the imperial rescript; the emperor wished to punish Hongxun by law, but Biao forcefully argued that the bribery charge was false.
translations.idiomatic: His colleague Liu Hongxun was impeached by Censor Wu Yu for altering an imperial rescript; the emperor wanted to punish Liu by law, but Biao insisted the bribery allegation was false.

sentences.zh: 溫體仁訐錢謙益引己結浙闈事為詞，給事中章允儒廷駁之。

translations.literal: Wen Tiren attacked Qian Qianyi, using as a pretext Qian's involving him in the Zhejiang metropolitan examination; Supervising Secretary Zhang Yunru rebutted him at court.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Tiren attacked Qian Qianyi on the pretext that Qian had drawn him into the Zhejiang metropolitan examination affair; Supervising Secretary Zhang Yunru refuted him in open court.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，並謙益將重譴，又欲罪給事中瞿式耜、御史房可壯等。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and was about to punish Qianyi heavily, and also wished to punish Supervising Secretary Qu Shisun, Censor Fang Kezhuang, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and was ready to punish Qianyi severely; he also wanted to punish Supervising Secretary Qu Shisun, Censor Fang Kezhuang, and others.

sentences.zh: 標言：「陛下處分謙益、允儒，本因體仁言，體仁乃不安求罷。

translations.literal: Biao said: "Your Majesty's handling of Qianyi and Yunru stems originally from Tiren's words; now Tiren is uneasy and seeks dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Biao said, "Your Majesty's treatment of Qianyi and Yunru began with Tiren's accusation, yet now Tiren himself is uneasy and asks to resign.

sentences.zh: 乞陛下念謙益事經恩詔，姑令回籍；

translations.literal: I beg Your Majesty to recall that Qianyi's case was already covered by an amnesty edict, and for the present let him return to his native place;
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to remember that Qianyi's case was already covered by an amnesty edict and for now let him return to his native place;

sentences.zh: 於允儒仍許自新，而式耜等概從薄罰。

translations.literal: as for Yunru, still permit him to reform, while Shisun and the rest receive only light punishment.
translations.idiomatic: allow Yunru a chance to reform, and impose only light penalties on Shisun and the rest.

sentences.zh: 諸臣安，體仁亦安。

translations.literal: All the officials will be at ease, and Tiren will be at ease too."
translations.idiomatic: The ministers will be settled, and Tiren will be settled as well."

sentences.zh: 」帝不從，自是深疑朝臣有黨，標等遂不得行其誌。

translations.literal: The emperor did not agree; from this he deeply suspected that court officials formed factions, and Biao and the others could no longer carry out their aims.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not agree. From then on he deeply suspected that court officials formed factions, and Biao and his colleagues could no longer put their plans into effect.

sentences.zh: 是冬，韓爌還朝，標讓為首輔，尋與爌等定逆案。

translations.literal: That winter Han Kuang returned to court; Biao yielded the chief ministership to him, and soon they with others settled the case of the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Han Kuang returned to court; Biao yielded the chief ministership to him, and soon joined him in settling the case of the rebels.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，爌罷，標復為首輔，累加至少保兼太子太保、戶部尚書、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year Han was dismissed and Biao again became chief grand secretary; he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year Han was dismissed and Biao again became chief grand secretary, eventually rising to Junior Guardian, concurrently Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Hall of Military Glory.

sentences.zh: 先是，與標並相者六人，宗道、景辰以附珰斥，鴻訓以增敕戍，周道登、錢龍錫被攻去，獨標在，遂五疏乞休。

translations.literal: Earlier, six men had served as grand secretaries together with Biao: Zongdao and Jingchen were expelled for adhering to the eunuch faction; Hongxun was banished for augmenting the rescript; Zhou Daodeng and Qian Longxi were attacked and left; only Biao remained, so he submitted five memorials begging retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, six men had served as grand secretaries alongside Biao: Zongdao and Jingchen were driven out for siding with the eunuch faction; Hongxun was banished for altering the rescript; Zhou Daodeng and Qian Longxi were hounded from office; only Biao remained, and he submitted five memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 至三月得請。

translations.literal: In the third month his request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 家居六年卒。

translations.literal: After six years at home he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home six years later.

sentences.zh: 贈少傅，謚文節。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed Junior Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenjie.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Junior Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenjie.

sentences.zh: 李國𣚴，字元治，高陽人。

translations.literal: Li Guogan, styled Yuanzhi, was a man of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guogan, whose style was Yuanzhi, came from Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年進士。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the forty-first year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士歷官詹事。

translations.literal: From bachelor he rose through the offices to Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin bachelor he rose through the ranks to Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 天啟六年七月，超擢禮部尚書入閣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year of Tianqi he was abruptly promoted to Minister of Rites and entered the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Tianqi 6 he was abruptly promoted to Minister of Rites and entered the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 釋褐十四年即登宰輔，魏忠賢以同鄉故援之也。

translations.literal: Having shed the scholar's robe for only fourteen years he reached the chief ministry—Wei Zhongxian promoted him because they were fellow-townsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Only fourteen years after leaving the scholar's robe he reached the chief ministry—Wei Zhongxian had backed him because they were from the same district.

sentences.zh: 然國𣚴每持正論。

translations.literal: Yet Guogan often upheld upright arguments.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Guogan often spoke on the side of right.

sentences.zh: 劉誌選劾張國紀以撼中宮，國𣚴言：「子不宜佐父難母，而況無間之父母乎！

translations.literal: Liu Zhixuan impeached Zhang Guoji to shake the empress; Guogan said: "A son ought not help his father against his mother—how much less parents between whom there is no estrangement!
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhixuan impeached Zhang Guoji in order to shake the empress; Guogan said, "A son should not help his father make trouble for his mother—how much less when the parents are not estranged!

sentences.zh: 」國紀乃得免罪。

translations.literal: " Zhang Guoji was thus spared punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Guoji was thus spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 御史方震孺及高陽令唐紹堯系獄，皆力為保全。

translations.literal: Censor Fang Zhenru and the Gaoyang magistrate Tang Shaoyao were imprisoned; he exerted himself to preserve them both.
translations.idiomatic: When Censor Fang Zhenru and the Gaoyang magistrate Tang Shaoyao were imprisoned, he worked hard to save them both.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，以登極恩進左柱國、少師兼太子太師、吏部尚書、中極殿大學士。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, under the enthronement grace he was advanced to Left Pillar of the State, Junior Tutor concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Central Peak Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongzhen, under the enthronement grace he was advanced to Left Pillar of the State, Junior Tutor concurrently Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, Minister of Personnel, and Grand Secretary of the Central Peak Hall.

sentences.zh: 國子監生胡煥猷劾國𣚴等褫衣冠，國普薦復之，時人稱為長厚。

translations.literal: The National University student Hu Huanyou impeached Guogan and others, stripping them of court dress; Guogan recommended their restoration, and contemporaries praised him as magnanimous.
translations.idiomatic: The National University student Hu Huanyou impeached Guogan and others and stripped them of court dress; Guogan recommended their restoration, and contemporaries praised his magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 元年五月得請歸裏，薦韓爌、孫承宗自代。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year he obtained leave to return home and recommended Han Kuang and Sun Chengzong to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the first year he obtained leave to return home and recommended Han Kuang and Sun Chengzong as his successors.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太保，謚文敏。

translations.literal: At death he was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: After his death he was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Tutor and given the posthumous title Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 宗道、景辰事見《黃立極傳》中。

translations.literal: Zongdao and Jingchen's affairs are recorded in the biography of Huang Liji.
translations.idiomatic: The affairs of Zongdao and Jingchen are recorded in the biography of Huang Liji.

sentences.zh: 周道登，吳江人。

translations.literal: Zhou Daodeng was a man of Wujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Daodeng came from Wujiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十六年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the twenty-sixth year of the Wanli reign.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士歷遷少詹事。

translations.literal: From bachelor he was promoted to Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin bachelor he rose to Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，為禮部左侍郎，頗有所爭執。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign he was Left Vice Minister of Rites and often entered disputes.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he served as Left Vice Minister of Rites and often took part in disputes.

sentences.zh: 以病歸。

translations.literal: He returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He went home on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 五年秋，廷推禮部尚書，魏忠賢削其籍。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year, when the court recommended candidates for Minister of Rites, Wei Zhongxian struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year, when the court recommended candidates for Minister of Rites, Wei Zhongxian struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，與李標等同入閣。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen he entered the Grand Secretariat together with Li Biao and others.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Chongzhen he entered the Grand Secretariat together with Li Biao and others.

sentences.zh: 道登無學術，奏對鄙淺，傳以為笑。

translations.literal: Daodeng had no learning; his responses at audience were crude and shallow, and the story became a laughingstock.
translations.idiomatic: Daodeng had no learning; his answers at audience were crude and shallow, and people passed the story around as a joke.

sentences.zh: 御史田時震、劉士禎、王道直、吳之仁、任贊化，給事中閻可陛交劾之，悉下廷議。

translations.literal: Censors Tian Shizhen, Liu Shizhen, Wang Daozhi, Wu Zhiren, and Ren Zanhua, and Supervising Secretary Yan Kedi jointly impeached him; all were referred to joint deliberation at court.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Tian Shizhen, Liu Shizhen, Wang Daozhi, Wu Zhiren, and Ren Zanhua, and Supervising Secretary Yan Kedi jointly impeached him; all cases were sent to joint deliberation at court.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書王永光等言道登黨護樞臣王在晉及宗生朱統飾、鄉人陳於鼎館選事，俱有實跡，乃罷歸。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang and others said Daodeng had factionally shielded Grand Secretary Wang Zaijin and the licentiate Zhu Tongshi, and fellow-townsman Chen Yuding in matters of examination appointments—all with verified facts—and he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang and others reported that Daodeng had factionally shielded Grand Secretary Wang Zaijin, the licentiate Zhu Tongshi, and his fellow townsman Chen Yuding in examination appointments—all with verified facts—and he was dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 閱五年而卒。

translations.literal: Five years later he died.
translations.idiomatic: Five years later he died.

sentences.zh: 劉鴻訓，字默承，長山人。

translations.literal: Liu Hongxun, styled Mocheng, was a man of Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongxun, whose style was Mocheng, came from Changshan.

sentences.zh: 父一相，由進士歷南京吏科給事中。

translations.literal: His father Yixiang, having become a jinshi, served as Supervising Secretary in the Nanjing Bureau of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yixiang, a jinshi, served as Supervising Secretary in the Nanjing Bureau of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 追論故相張居正事，執政忌之，出為隴右僉事。

translations.literal: He pursued judgment on the late Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng's case; the ruling faction resented him and he was sent out as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued judgment on the late Grand Secretary Zhang Juzheng's case; the ruling faction resented him and he was sent out as Assistant Surveillance Commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 終陜西副使。

translations.literal: He ended as Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Vice Commissioner of Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十一年，鴻訓登第，由庶吉士授編修。

translations.literal: In the forty-first year of Wanli, Hongxun passed the examination; from bachelor he was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: In the forty-first year of Wanli, Hongxun passed the examination; from Hanlin bachelor he was appointed compiler.

sentences.zh: 神、光二宗相繼崩，頒詔朝鮮。

translations.literal: The Shenzong and Guangzong emperors died in succession, and edicts were promulgated in Korea.
translations.idiomatic: The Shenzong and Guangzong emperors died in succession, and edicts were promulgated in Korea.

sentences.zh: 甫入境，遼陽陷。

translations.literal: He had barely entered the border when Liaoyang fell.
translations.idiomatic: He had barely crossed the border when Liaoyang fell.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮為造二洋舶，從海道還。

translations.literal: Korea built two ocean-going ships for him, and he returned by sea.
translations.idiomatic: Korea built two ocean-going ships for him, and he returned by sea.

sentences.zh: 沿途收難民，舶重而壞。

translations.literal: Along the way he took aboard refugees; the ships grew heavy and were wrecked.
translations.idiomatic: Along the way he took aboard refugees; the ships grew heavy and were wrecked.

sentences.zh: 跳淺沙，入小舟，飄泊三日夜，僅得達登州報命。

translations.literal: He waded through shallows into small boats and drifted three days and nights, barely reaching Dengzhou to report his mission fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: He waded through shallows into small boats and drifted for three days and nights, barely reaching Dengzhou to report his mission complete.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，服闋，進右中允，轉左諭德，父喪歸。

translations.literal: He encountered his mother's mourning; when the mourning period ended he was promoted Right Middle Gentleman-for-Instruction, then transferred Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and returned home for his father's mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He mourned his mother; when the mourning period ended he was promoted to Right Middle Gentleman-for-Instruction, then transferred to Left Tutor of the Heir Apparent, and returned home for his father's mourning.

sentences.zh: 天啟六年冬，起少詹事，忤魏忠賢，斥為民。

translations.literal: In the winter of the sixth year of Tianqi he was recalled as Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent; he offended Wei Zhongxian and was dismissed to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of Tianqi 6 he was recalled as Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent; he offended Wei Zhongxian and was reduced to commoner status.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，參預機務，遣行人召之。

translations.literal: When the Chongzhen Emperor ascended the throne, Hongxun was appointed Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, participating in state affairs; an emissary was sent to summon him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chongzhen Emperor took the throne, Hongxun was appointed Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, with a role in state affairs; an emissary was sent to summon him.

sentences.zh: 三辭，不允。

translations.literal: He declined three times but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He declined three times but was not allowed to refuse.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年四月還朝。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Chongzhen he returned to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Chongzhen 1 he returned to court.

sentences.zh: 當是時，忠賢雖敗，其黨猶盛，言路新進者群起抨擊之。

translations.literal: At that time although Zhongxian had fallen, his faction remained strong, and newly risen critics at the censorate attacked in groups.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, although Zhongxian had fallen, his faction was still strong, and newly risen critics at the censorate attacked in groups.

sentences.zh: 諸執政嘗與忠賢共事，不敢顯為別白。

translations.literal: The chief ministers had once served together with Zhongxian and dared not openly distinguish right from wrong.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers had once served with Zhongxian and dared not openly set the record straight.

sentences.zh: 鴻訓至，毅然主持，斥楊維垣、李恒茂、楊所修、田景新、孫之獬、阮大鋮、徐紹吉、張訥、李蕃、賈繼春、霍維華等，人情大快。

translations.literal: When Hongxun arrived he boldly took charge, denouncing Yang Weiyuan, Li Hengmao, Yang Suoxiu, Tian Jingxin, Sun Zhixi, Ruan Dayue, Xu Shaoji, Zhang Na, Li Fan, Jia Jichun, Huo Weihua, and others—to general rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: When Hongxun arrived he took charge resolutely, denouncing Yang Weiyuan, Li Hengmao, Yang Suoxiu, Tian Jingxin, Sun Zhixi, Ruan Dayue, Xu Shaoji, Zhang Na, Li Fan, Jia Jichun, Huo Weihua, and others—to widespread satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 而御史袁弘勛、史褵、高捷本由維垣輩進，思合謀攻去鴻訓，則黨人可安也。

translations.literal: Yet Censors Yuan Hongxun, Shi Li, and Gao Jie had originally advanced through Weiyuan's party and thought to unite in attacking Hongxun so the faction could be secure.
translations.idiomatic: But Censors Yuan Hongxun, Shi Li, and Gao Jie had originally risen through Weiyuan's faction and thought to join forces to drive Hongxun out so their party could rest easy.

sentences.zh: 弘勛乃言所修、繼春、維垣夾攻表裏之奸，有功無罪，而誅鋤自三臣始；

translations.literal: Hongxun then said Suoxiu, Jichun, and Weiyuan had exposed inner and outer traitors and were meritorious without guilt, while the purge began with these three ministers;
translations.idiomatic: Hongxun then argued that Suoxiu, Jichun, and Weiyuan had exposed traitors within and without, were meritorious and guiltless, and that the purge had wrongly begun with these three ministers;

sentences.zh: 又詆鴻訓使朝鮮，滿載貂參而歸。

translations.literal: he also slandered Hongxun's mission to Korea, saying he returned laden with sable and ginseng.
translations.idiomatic: he also slandered Hongxun's mission to Korea, claiming he returned laden with sable and ginseng.

sentences.zh: 錦衣僉事張道浚亦訐攻鴻訓，鴻訓奏辯。

translations.literal: Assistant Commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard Zhang Daojun also impeached Hongxun; Hongxun memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Commander of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard Zhang Daojun also impeached Hongxun; Hongxun memorialized in his own defense.

sentences.zh: 給事中顏繼祖言：「鴻訓先朝削奪。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yan Jizu said: "Hongxun was demoted and stripped in the previous dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yan Jizu said, "Hongxun was demoted and stripped of rank in the previous reign.

sentences.zh: 朝鮮一役，舟敗，僅以身免。

translations.literal: In the Korea campaign his boats were defeated, and he barely escaped with his own person.
translations.idiomatic: In the Korea campaign his fleet was defeated, and he barely escaped with his life.

sentences.zh: 乞諭鴻訓入直，共籌安攘之策。

translations.literal: I beg that Hongxun be instructed to enter direct service and jointly devise policies for pacification and repelling the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Hongxun be summoned to direct service so we may jointly devise policies for pacification and defense.

sentences.zh: 至弘勛之借題傾人，道浚之出位亂政，非重創未有已也。

translations.literal: As for Hongxun's using pretexts to topple others and Daojun's overstepping his office to disrupt government, unless they are severely punished it will not end.
translations.idiomatic: As for Hongxun's habit of seizing on any pretext to ruin others and Daojun's overstepping his station to disrupt government, unless they are severely punished there will be no end to it.

sentences.zh: 」帝是之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor approved this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 給事中鄧英乃盡發弘勛贓私，且言弘勛以千金贄維垣得御史。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Deng Ying then fully exposed Hongxun's corrupt dealings, and also said Hongxun had obtained the post of censor by presenting Weiyuan with a thousand taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Deng Ying then fully exposed Hongxun's corruption, and also charged that Hongxun had bought his censor's post with a thousand taels of gold paid to Weiyuan.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，落弘勛職候勘。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and stripped Hongxun of his post pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and dismissed Hongxun from office pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 已而高捷上疏言鴻訓斥擊奸之維垣、所修、繼春、大鋮，而不納孫之獬流涕忠言；

translations.literal: Before long Gao Jie memorialized, saying Hongxun had attacked the traitors Weiyuan, Suoxiu, Jichun, and Dayue, yet had not accepted Sun Zhixi's tearful loyal advice;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Gao Jie memorialized, charging that Hongxun had attacked the traitors Weiyuan, Suoxiu, Jichun, and Dayue while refusing to heed Sun Zhixi's tearful loyal counsel;

sentences.zh: 謬主焚毀《要典》，以便私黨孫慎行進用。

translations.literal: he had wrongly advocated burning the Compendium of Essentials so that his private clique member Sun Shenxing could be advanced.
translations.idiomatic: he had wrongly advocated burning the Compendium of Essentials so that his private ally Sun Shenxing could be promoted.

sentences.zh: 帝責以妄言，停其俸。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him for reckless speech and suspended his salary.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor rebuked him for reckless speech and suspended his salary.

sentences.zh: 史褷復佐捷攻之。

translations.literal: Shi Li again aided Jie in attacking him.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Li again joined Jie in attacking him.

sentences.zh: 言路多不直兩人，兩人遂罷去。

translations.literal: Most of the censorate did not support the two men, and the two were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Most of the censorate did not side with the two men, and both were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 七月，以四川賊平，加鴻訓太子太保，進文淵閣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, because the Sichuan bandits were pacified, Hongxun was promoted to Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, with the Sichuan rebels pacified, Hongxun was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and entered the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝數召見廷臣。

translations.literal: The Emperor frequently summoned court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor frequently summoned court ministers for audience.

sentences.zh: 鴻訓應對獨敏，謂民困由吏失職，請帝久任責成。

translations.literal: Hongxun answered with especial quickness, saying the people's hardship came from officials' dereliction of duty, and asked the Emperor to appoint men for long terms and hold them accountable.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxun answered with unusual quickness, arguing that the people's hardship stemmed from officials' dereliction of duty, and urging the Emperor to keep men in office long enough to hold them accountable.

sentences.zh: 以尚書畢自嚴善治賦，王在晉善治兵，請帝加倚信。

translations.literal: Saying that Ministers Bi Ziyan was skilled at managing taxation and Wang Zaijin at managing troops, he asked the Emperor to rely on them more.
translations.idiomatic: Noting that Minister Bi Ziyan was skilled at managing taxation and Wang Zaijin at managing troops, he asked the Emperor to place greater trust in them.

sentences.zh: 帝初甚向之。

translations.literal: At first the Emperor was very disposed toward him.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Emperor was strongly inclined toward him.

sentences.zh: 關門兵以缺餉鼓噪，帝意責戶部，而鴻訓請發帑三十萬，示不測恩，由是失帝指。

translations.literal: Soldiers at Shanhaiguan clamored over unpaid rations; the Emperor intended to blame the Ministry of Revenue, but Hongxun requested disbursing three hundred thousand taels from the treasury to show unlooked-for favor, and thereby lost the Emperor's goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers at Shanhaiguan clamored over unpaid rations; the Emperor meant to blame the Ministry of Revenue, but Hongxun asked to disburse three hundred thousand taels from the treasury as an unexpected favor, and thereby lost the Emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 至九月而有改敕書之事。

translations.literal: By the ninth month there arose the matter of altering an imperial edict.
translations.idiomatic: By the ninth month the affair of altering an imperial edict had arisen.

sentences.zh: 舊例，督京營者，不轄巡捕軍。

translations.literal: By old precedent, whoever supervised the capital garrison did not command the patrol and arrest troops.
translations.idiomatic: By established precedent, the supervisor of the capital garrison did not command the patrol and arrest troops.

sentences.zh: 惠安伯張慶臻總督京營，敕有「兼轄捕營」語，提督鄭其心以侵職論之。

translations.literal: The Earl of Huian, Zhang Qingzhen, supervised the capital garrison; the edict contained the phrase "also commanding the patrol battalion," and Superintendent Zheng Qixin charged this as an encroachment on his duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Earl of Huian, Zhang Qingzhen, supervised the capital garrison, but the edict contained the phrase "also commanding the patrol battalion," and Superintendent Zheng Qixin charged this as an encroachment on his authority.

sentences.zh: 命核中書賄改之故，下舍人田佳璧獄。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered an investigation into how the Secretariat had been bribed to alter the edict, and imprisoned the drafter Tian Jiabi.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered an investigation into how the Secretariat had been bribed to alter the edict, and imprisoned the drafter Tian Jiabi.

sentences.zh: 給事中李覺斯言：「稿具兵部，送輔臣裁定，乃令中書繕寫。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Li Juesi said: "The draft was prepared by the Ministry of War, sent to the chief ministers for approval, and only then ordered copied by the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Li Juesi said, "The draft was prepared by the Ministry of War, sent to the chief ministers for approval, and only then ordered copied by the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 寫訖，復審視進呈。

translations.literal: When copying was finished, it was reviewed again before submission.
translations.idiomatic: Once copying was finished, it was reviewed again before being submitted.

sentences.zh: 兵部及輔臣皆當問。

translations.literal: Both the Ministry of War and the chief ministers should be questioned.
translations.idiomatic: Both the Ministry of War and the chief ministers should be questioned.

sentences.zh: 」十月，帝御便殿，問閣臣，皆謝不知。

translations.literal: " In the tenth month the Emperor held court in the side hall and questioned the Grand Secretaries; all apologized that they did not know.
translations.idiomatic: " In the tenth month the Emperor held audience in the side hall and questioned the Grand Secretaries; all pleaded ignorance.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，令廷臣劾奏；

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered and ordered court ministers to impeach and report;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged and ordered court ministers to impeach and report;

sentences.zh: 尚書自嚴等亦謝不知，帝益怒。

translations.literal: Minister Bi Ziyan and the others also apologized that they did not know, and the Emperor grew still angrier.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Bi Ziyan and the others also pleaded ignorance, and the Emperor grew still angrier.

sentences.zh: 給事中張鼎延、御史王道直鹹言慶臻行賄有跡，不知誰主使。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Zhang Dingyan and Censor Wang Daozhi also said there were traces of bribery by Qingzhen, but they did not know who had instigated it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Zhang Dingyan and Censor Wang Daozhi also said there was evidence that Qingzhen had paid bribes, though they did not know who had instigated it.

sentences.zh: 御史劉玉言：「主使者，鴻訓也。

translations.literal: Censor Liu Yu said: "The instigator was Hongxun.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Liu Yu said, "The instigator was Hongxun.

sentences.zh: 」慶臻曰：「改敕乃中書事，臣實不預知。

translations.literal: " Qingzhen said: "Altering the edict was a matter for the Secretariat; your subject truly had no foreknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: " Qingzhen said, "Altering the edict was a matter for the Secretariat; I truly had no foreknowledge.

sentences.zh: 且增轄捕卒，取利幾何，乃行重賄？

translations.literal: Moreover, what profit could there be in adding command over a few patrol soldiers, that one would pay a heavy bribe?
translations.idiomatic: Besides, what profit could there be in adding command over a few patrol soldiers, that one would pay a heavy bribe?

sentences.zh: 」帝叱之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 閱兵部揭有鴻訓批西司房語，佳璧亦供受鴻訓指，事遂不可解，而侍郎張鳳翔詆之尤力。

translations.literal: On examining the Ministry of War memorial there were words in Hongxun's hand from the West Office; Jiabi also confessed to acting on Hongxun's instructions, and the matter became impossible to explain away, while Vice Minister Zhang Fengxiang denounced him with especial force.
translations.idiomatic: On examining the Ministry of War memorial there were words in Hongxun's hand from the West Office; Jiabi also confessed to acting on Hongxun's orders, and the matter became impossible to explain away, while Vice Minister Zhang Fengxiang denounced him with especial force.

sentences.zh: 閣臣李標、錢龍錫言鴻訓不宜有此，請更察訪。

translations.literal: Grand Secretaries Li Biao and Qian Longxi said Hongxun ought not to have done this and asked for further investigation.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretaries Li Biao and Qian Longxi said Hongxun ought not to have done this and asked for further investigation.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「事已大著，何更訪為？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The matter is already fully exposed—why investigate further?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The matter is already fully exposed—why investigate further?

sentences.zh: 」促令擬旨。

translations.literal: " He pressed them to draft the rescript.
translations.idiomatic: " He pressed them to draft the rescript.

sentences.zh: 標等逡巡未上，禮部尚書何如寵為鴻訓力辯，帝意卒不可回。

translations.literal: Biao and the others hesitated and did not submit; Minister of Rites He Ruchong argued forcefully for Hongxun, but the Emperor's mind could not in the end be turned.
translations.idiomatic: Biao and the others hesitated and did not submit; Minister of Rites He Ruchong argued forcefully for Hongxun, but the Emperor's mind could not in the end be changed.

sentences.zh: 乃擬旨，鴻訓、慶臻並革職候勘。

translations.literal: They then drafted the rescript: Hongxun and Qingzhen were both stripped of office pending investigation.
translations.idiomatic: They then drafted the rescript: Hongxun and Qingzhen were both stripped of office pending investigation.

sentences.zh: 無何，御史田時震劾鴻訓用田仰巡撫四川，納賄二千金；

translations.literal: Before long Censor Tian Shizhen impeached Hongxun for appointing Tian Yang as Sichuan governor after accepting a bribe of two thousand taels;
translations.idiomatic: Before long Censor Tian Shizhen impeached Hongxun for appointing Tian Yang governor of Sichuan after accepting a bribe of two thousand taels;

sentences.zh: 給事中閻可陛劾副都御史賈毓祥由賂鴻訓擢用。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Yan Keshou impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Jia Yuxiang for having been promoted through bribing Hongxun.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Yan Keshou impeached Vice Censor-in-Chief Jia Yuxiang for having been promoted through bribes paid to Hongxun.

sentences.zh: 鴻訓數被劾，連章力辯，因言「都中神奸狄姓者，詭誆慶臻千金，致臣無辜受禍。

translations.literal: Hongxun was impeached repeatedly and memorialized again and again in forceful defense, saying: "In the capital there is a sinister schemer surnamed Di who deceived Qingzhen out of a thousand taels and caused your subject to suffer punishment without guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxun was impeached repeatedly and memorialized again and again in his own defense, saying, "In the capital there is a sinister schemer surnamed Di who tricked Qingzhen out of a thousand taels and caused me to suffer punishment without guilt.

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽，下廷臣議罪。

translations.literal: " The Emperor would not listen and referred the matter to court ministers to determine punishment.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor would not listen and referred the matter to court ministers to determine punishment.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，吏部尚書王永光等言：「鴻訓、慶臻罪無可辭，而律有議貴條，請寬貸。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang and others said: "Hongxun and Qingzhen are guilty beyond excuse, but the law has a provision for deliberating on the punishment of the eminent— we ask for leniency.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year Minister of Personnel Wang Yongguang and others said, "Hongxun and Qingzhen are guilty beyond excuse, but the law has a provision for deliberating on the punishment of the eminent—we ask for leniency.

sentences.zh: 兵部尚書王在晉、職方郎中苗思順贓證未確，難懸坐。

translations.literal: Minister of War Wang Zaijin and Bureau Director Miao Sishun lack firm evidence of corruption and cannot be condemned on suspicion alone.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of War Wang Zaijin and Bureau Director Miao Sishun lack firm evidence of corruption and cannot be condemned on suspicion alone.

sentences.zh: 」帝不許。

translations.literal: " The Emperor did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 鴻訓謫戍代州，在晉、思順並削籍，慶臻以世臣停祿三年。

translations.literal: Hongxun was banished to garrison duty at Daizhou; Zaijin and Sishun were both struck from the rolls; Qingzhen, as a hereditary minister, had his salary suspended for three years.
translations.idiomatic: Hongxun was banished to garrison duty at Daizhou; Zaijin and Sishun were both struck from the rolls; Qingzhen, as a hereditary minister, had his salary suspended for three years.

sentences.zh: 覺斯、鼎延、道直、玉、時震以直言增秩一級。

translations.literal: Juesi, Dingyan, Daozhi, Yu, and Shizhen were each promoted one rank for their forthright speech.
translations.idiomatic: Juesi, Dingyan, Daozhi, Yu, and Shizhen were each promoted one rank for their forthright speech.

sentences.zh: 鴻訓居政府，銳意任事。

translations.literal: While Hongxun held office in the government he was keen to take on affairs.
translations.idiomatic: While Hongxun served in government he was keen to take charge of affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝有所不可，退而曰：「主上畢竟是沖主。

translations.literal: When the Emperor disapproved of something, he would withdraw and say: "After all, the sovereign is still a young ruler.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor disapproved of something, he would withdraw and say, "After all, the sovereign is still a young and emerging ruler.

sentences.zh: 」帝聞，深銜之，欲置之死。

translations.literal: " When the Emperor heard this he deeply resented it and wished to put him to death.
translations.idiomatic: " When the Emperor heard this he deeply resented it and wished to have him executed.

sentences.zh: 賴諸大臣力救，乃得稍寬。

translations.literal: Only through the chief ministers' forceful intercession was the punishment somewhat lightened.
translations.idiomatic: Only through the chief ministers' forceful intercession was the punishment somewhat lightened.

sentences.zh: 七年五月卒戍所。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the seventh year he died at his place of exile.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the seventh year he died in exile.

sentences.zh: 福王時，復官。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu his office was restored.

sentences.zh: 錢龍錫，字稚文，松江華亭人。

translations.literal: Qian Longxi, courtesy name Zhiwen, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Longxi, courtesy name Zhiwen, was a native of Huating in Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in Wanli 35.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授編修，屢遷少詹事。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Compiler and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin Bachelor he was appointed Compiler and was repeatedly promoted to Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 天啟四年擢禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Tianqi he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and assisted in managing the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 4 he was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites and assisted in managing the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 明年改南京吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: The following year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 忤魏忠賢，削籍。

translations.literal: He offended Wei Zhongxian and was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He offended Wei Zhongxian and was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 莊烈帝即位，以閣臣黃立極、施鳳來、張瑞圖、李國𣚴皆忠賢所用，不足倚，詔廷臣推舉，列上十人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuanglie ascended the throne, because Grand Secretaries Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, Zhang Ruitu, and Li Guo'an had all been men used by Zhongxian and were not to be relied on, he ordered court ministers to recommend candidates and ten names were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuanglie ascended the throne, because Grand Secretaries Huang Liji, Shi Fenglai, Zhang Ruitu, and Li Guo'an had all been men used by Zhongxian and could not be relied on, he ordered court ministers to recommend candidates and ten names were submitted.

sentences.zh: 帝仿古枚卜典，貯名金甌，焚香肅拜，以次探之，首得龍錫，次李標、來宗道、楊景辰。

translations.literal: The Emperor followed the ancient lot-drawing rite: names were stored in a golden urn; after burning incense and bowing reverently he drew them in order—Longxi came first, then Li Biao, Lai Zongdao, and Yang Jingchen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor followed the ancient lot-drawing rite: names were stored in a golden urn; after burning incense and bowing reverently he drew them in order—Longxi came first, then Li Biao, Lai Zongdao, and Yang Jingchen.

sentences.zh: 輔臣以天下多故，請益一二人，復得周道登、劉鴻訓，並拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士。

translations.literal: The chief ministers, citing the many troubles in the realm, asked that one or two more be added; Zhou Daodeng and Liu Hongxun were also chosen, and all were appointed Ministers of Rites and Grand Secretaries of the Eastern Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The chief ministers, citing the many troubles in the realm, asked that one or two more be added; Zhou Daodeng and Liu Hongxun were also chosen, and all were appointed Ministers of Rites and Grand Secretaries of the Eastern Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，龍錫入朝，立極等四人俱先罷，宗道、景辰亦以是月去。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the following year Longxi entered court; Liji and the other four had all been dismissed earlier, and Zongdao and Jingchen also left that same month.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the following year Longxi entered court; Liji and the other four had all been dismissed earlier, and Zongdao and Jingchen also left that same month.

sentences.zh: 標為首輔，龍錫、鴻訓協心輔理，朝政稍清。

translations.literal: Biao became chief minister; Longxi and Hongxun worked together in governing, and court affairs grew somewhat clearer.
translations.idiomatic: Biao became chief minister; Longxi and Hongxun worked together in governing, and court affairs grew somewhat clearer.

sentences.zh: 尋以蜀寇平，加太子太保，改文淵閣。

translations.literal: Soon, because the Sichuan rebels were pacified, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, with the Sichuan rebels pacified, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and transferred to the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 帝好察邊事，頻遣旗尉偵探。

translations.literal: The Emperor liked to investigate border affairs and frequently sent banner guards as spies.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor liked to investigate border affairs and frequently sent banner guards as spies.

sentences.zh: 龍錫言：「舊制止行於都城內外，若遠遣恐難委信。

translations.literal: Longxi said: "The old prohibition applied only within and around the capital; if men are sent far away, I fear they will be hard to trust.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi said, "The old prohibition applied only within and around the capital; if men are sent far away, I fear they will be hard to trust.

sentences.zh: 」海寇犯中左所，總兵官俞咨臯棄城遁，罪當誅。

translations.literal: " Sea bandits attacked Zhongzuo Station; Regional Commander Yu Zigao abandoned the city and fled—the crime deserved execution.
translations.idiomatic: " Sea bandits attacked Zhongzuo Station; Regional Commander Yu Zigao abandoned the city and fled—a crime deserving execution.

sentences.zh: 帝欲並罪巡撫朱一馮。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished also to punish Governor Zhu Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished also to punish Governor Zhu Yifeng.

sentences.zh: 龍錫言：「一馮所駐遠，非棄城者比，罷職已足蔽辜。

translations.literal: Longxi said: "Yifeng's post was far away; he cannot be compared with one who abandoned the city—dismissal from office is enough to cover the fault.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi said, "Yifeng's post was far away; he cannot be compared with one who abandoned the city—dismissal from office is enough to answer for the fault.

sentences.zh: 」瑞王出封漢中，請食川鹽。

translations.literal: " Prince Rui, upon receiving his fief at Hanzhong, requested to consume Sichuan salt.
translations.idiomatic: " When Prince Rui received his fief at Hanzhong, he requested to consume Sichuan salt.

sentences.zh: 龍錫言：「漢中食晉鹽，而瑞藩獨用川鹽，恐奸徒借名私販，莫敢譏察。

translations.literal: Longxi said: "Hanzhong consumes Jin salt, yet the Prince of Rui alone would use Sichuan salt—I fear scoundrels would use his name to smuggle salt privately, and no one would dare investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi said, "Hanzhong consumes Jin salt, yet Prince Rui alone would use Sichuan salt—I fear scoundrels would trade on his name to smuggle salt privately, and no one would dare investigate.

sentences.zh: 」故事，纂修實錄，分遣國學生采事跡於四方，龍錫言「實錄所需在邸報及諸司奏牘，遣使無益，徒滋擾，宜停罷。

translations.literal: " By precedent, when compiling the Veritable Records, Imperial University students were dispatched to gather materials in all directions; Longxi said: "What the Veritable Records require is found in the Gazette and in memorials from the various offices—sending envoys is useless and only creates disturbance; this should be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " By precedent, when compiling the Veritable Records, Imperial University students were dispatched to gather materials throughout the realm; Longxi said, "What the Veritable Records require is found in the Gazette and in memorials from the various offices—sending envoys is useless and only creates disturbance; this should be stopped.

sentences.zh: 」烏撒土官安效良死，其妻改適沾益土官安邊，欲兼有烏撒，部議將聽之。

translations.literal: " The native chieftain An Xiaoliang of Wusa died; his wife remarried An Bian, chieftain of Zhanyi, who wished to take Wusa as well; the ministry deliberated and was about to approve.
translations.idiomatic: " The native chieftain An Xiaoliang of Wusa died; his wife remarried An Bian, chieftain of Zhanyi, who wished to take Wusa as well; the ministry deliberated and was about to approve.

sentences.zh: 龍錫言：「效良有子其爵，立其爵以收烏撒，存亡繼絕，於理為順。

translations.literal: Longxi said: "Xiaoliang had a son, Qi Jue—install Qi Jue to recover Wusa; preserving what was endangered and continuing what was broken off is in accord with principle.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi said, "Xiaoliang had a son, Qi Jue—install Qi Jue to recover Wusa; preserving what was endangered and continuing what was broken off is in accord with principle.

sentences.zh: 安邊淫亂，不可長也。

translations.literal: An Bian is licentious and disorderly and must not be indulged.
translations.idiomatic: An Bian is licentious and disorderly and must not be indulged.

sentences.zh: 」帝悉從之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor fully agreed.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor fully agreed.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝以漕船違禁越關，欲復設漕運總兵官。

translations.literal: The following year, because grain-transport ships had violated prohibitions and passed through customs, the Emperor wished to restore the post of Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, because grain-transport ships had violated prohibitions and passed through customs, the Emperor wished to restore the post of Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport.

sentences.zh: 龍錫言：「久裁而復，宜集廷臣議得失。

translations.literal: Longxi said: "This office was abolished long ago and would now be restored—it is fitting to gather court ministers to discuss its advantages and disadvantages.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi said, "This office was abolished long ago and would now be restored—it is fitting to gather court ministers to discuss its advantages and disadvantages.

sentences.zh: 」事竟止。

translations.literal: " The matter was dropped in the end.
translations.idiomatic: " The matter was dropped in the end.

sentences.zh: 廷議汰冗官，帝謂學官尤冗。

translations.literal: At court they debated eliminating redundant offices; the Emperor said educational officials were especially redundant.
translations.idiomatic: At court they debated eliminating redundant offices; the Emperor said educational officials were especially redundant.

sentences.zh: 龍錫言：「學官舊用歲貢生，近因舉人乞恩選貢，纂修占缺者多，歲貢積至二千六百有奇，皓首以歿，良可憫。

translations.literal: Longxi said: "Educational posts were formerly filled from annual tribute students; recently, because licentiates begged favors and were selected as tribute students, many took vacancies reserved for compilation work, and annual tribute students accumulated to more than twenty-six hundred—white-haired men dying in office, truly pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi said, "Educational posts were formerly filled from annual tribute students; recently, because licentiates begged favors and were selected as tribute students, many took vacancies reserved for compilation work, and annual tribute students accumulated to more than twenty-six hundred—white-haired men dying in office, truly pitiable.

sentences.zh: 且祖宗設官，於此稍寬者，以師儒造士需老成故也。

translations.literal: Moreover, in establishing these offices our forefathers were somewhat lenient because teachers who cultivate scholars require maturity.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in establishing these offices our forefathers were somewhat lenient because teachers who cultivate scholars require maturity.

sentences.zh: 」帝亦納之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor also accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor also accepted this.

sentences.zh: 言官鄒毓祚、韓一良、章允儒、劉斯來獲譴，並為申救。

translations.literal: Censors Zou Yuzuo, Han Yiliang, Zhang Yunru, and Liu Silai were punished, and he interceded for them all.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Zou Yuzuo, Han Yiliang, Zhang Yunru, and Liu Silai were punished, and he interceded for them all.

sentences.zh: 御史高捷、史褷既罷，王永光力引之，頗為龍錫所扼，兩人大恨。

translations.literal: After Censors Gao Jie and Shi Li were dismissed, Wang Yongguang worked hard to bring them back, but Longxi largely blocked them, and the two men deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: After Censors Gao Jie and Shi Li were dismissed, Wang Yongguang worked hard to bring them back, but Longxi largely blocked them, and the two men deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 逆案之定，半為龍錫主持，奸黨銜之次骨。

translations.literal: In settling the case of the traitors, Longxi had presided over half of it, and the villainous faction hated him to the marrow.
translations.idiomatic: In settling the case of the traitors, Longxi had presided over half of it, and the villainous faction hated him to the marrow.

sentences.zh: 及袁崇煥殺毛文龍，報疏云：「輔臣龍錫為此一事低徊過臣寓。

translations.literal: When Yuan Chonghuan killed Mao Wenlong, his report said: "Chief Minister Longxi lingered at my residence over this matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chonghuan killed Mao Wenlong, his report said, "Chief Minister Longxi lingered at my residence over this matter.

sentences.zh: 」復上善後疏言：「閣臣樞臣，往復商確，臣以是得奉行無失。

translations.literal: " He then submitted a follow-up memorial on handling the aftermath, saying: "The Grand Secretaries and the minister of war discussed back and forth, and your subject was thereby able to carry out the orders without error.
translations.idiomatic: " He then submitted a follow-up memorial on handling the aftermath, saying, "The Grand Secretaries and the minister of war discussed back and forth, and I was thereby able to carry out the orders without error.

sentences.zh: 」時文龍擁兵自擅，有跋扈聲，崇煥一旦除之，即當寧不以為罪也。

translations.literal: " At the time Wenlong held troops and acted on his own authority, with a reputation for arrogance; that Chonghuan removed him at a stroke ought not to have been treated as a crime by the throne.
translations.idiomatic: " At the time Wenlong held troops and acted on his own authority, with a reputation for arrogance; that Chonghuan removed him at a stroke ought not to have been treated as a crime by the throne.

sentences.zh: 其冬十二月，大清兵薄都城。

translations.literal: That winter, in the twelfth month, the Great Qing army pressed close to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, in the twelfth month, the Great Qing army pressed close to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝怒崇煥戰不力，執下獄，而捷、褷已為永光引用。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angered that Chonghuan had not fought vigorously and had him arrested and imprisoned; by then Jie and Li had already been brought back by Yongguang.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was enraged that Chonghuan had not fought vigorously and had him arrested and imprisoned; by then Jie and Li had already been brought back by Yongguang.

sentences.zh: 捷遂上章，指通款殺將為龍錫罪，且言祖大壽師潰而東，由龍錫所挑激。

translations.literal: Jie then memorialized, charging that colluding with the enemy and killing a general were Longxi's crimes, and also saying that Zu Dashou's army had collapsed and fled east because Longxi had provoked it.
translations.idiomatic: Jie then memorialized, charging that colluding with the enemy and killing a general were Longxi's crimes, and also saying that Zu Dashou's army had collapsed and fled east because Longxi had provoked it.

sentences.zh: 帝以龍錫忠慎，戒無過求。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering Longxi loyal and cautious, warned against pressing the charges too far.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, considering Longxi loyal and cautious, warned against pressing the charges too far.

sentences.zh: 龍錫奏辯，言：「崇煥陛見時，臣見其貌寢，退謂同官『此人恐不勝任』。

translations.literal: Longxi memorialized in defense, saying: "When Chonghuan had audience, your subject saw that his appearance was poor and withdrew, telling a colleague, 'This man may not be up to the task.'
translations.idiomatic: Longxi memorialized in his defense, saying, "When Chonghuan had audience, I saw that his appearance was poor and withdrew, telling a colleague, 'This man may not be up to the task.'

sentences.zh: 及崇煥以五年復遼自詭，往詢方略，崇煥云：『恢復當自東江始。

translations.literal: When Chonghuan boasted that he would recover Liaodong within five years, your subject went to ask his strategy; Chonghuan said: 'Recovery should begin from the Eastern Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Chonghuan boasted that he would recover Liaodong within five years, I went to ask his strategy; Chonghuan said, 'Recovery should begin from the Eastern Jiang.

sentences.zh: 文龍可用則用之，不可用則去之易易耳。

translations.literal: If Wenlong can be used, use him; if not, remove him—easily done.'
translations.idiomatic: If Wenlong can be used, use him; if not, remove him—easily done.'

sentences.zh: 』迨崇煥突誅文龍，疏有『臣低徊』一語。

translations.literal: ' When Chonghuan suddenly executed Wenlong, his memorial contained the phrase 'your subject lingered.'
translations.idiomatic: ' When Chonghuan suddenly executed Wenlong, his memorial contained the phrase 'I lingered.'

sentences.zh: 臣念文龍功罪，朝端共知，因置不理。

translations.literal: Your subject considered Wenlong's merits and faults, which everyone at court knew, and therefore set the matter aside.
translations.idiomatic: I considered Wenlong's merits and faults, which everyone at court knew, and therefore set the matter aside.

sentences.zh: 奈何以崇煥誇詡之詞，坐臣朋謀罪？

translations.literal: How then can your subject be convicted of conspiracy on the strength of Chonghuan's boastful words?
translations.idiomatic: How then can I be convicted of conspiracy on the strength of Chonghuan's boastful words?

sentences.zh: 」又辯挑激大壽之誣，請賜罷黜。

translations.literal: " He also rebutted the false charge of having provoked Dashou, and asked to be dismissed and removed.
translations.idiomatic: He also rebutted the false charge that he had provoked Dashou, and asked to be dismissed.

sentences.zh: 帝慰諭之，龍錫即起視事。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted and instructed him, and Longxi immediately rose to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor reassured him, and Longxi at once returned to office.

sentences.zh: 捷再疏攻，帝意頗動。

translations.literal: Jie memorialized attacking again; the Emperor's mind was quite moved.
translations.idiomatic: Jie attacked again in a further memorial, and the Emperor was substantially swayed.

sentences.zh: 龍錫再辯，引疾，遂放歸。

translations.literal: Longxi defended himself again, pleaded illness, and was finally released to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi memorialized in his defense once more, then pleaded illness and was sent home.

sentences.zh: 時兵事旁午，未暇竟崇煥獄。

translations.literal: At the time military affairs pressed from all sides; there was no leisure to conclude Chonghuan's case.
translations.idiomatic: Military crises were pressing on all sides, and there was no time to bring Chonghuan's case to a conclusion.

sentences.zh: 至三年八月，褷復上疏言：「龍錫主張崇煥斬帥致兵，倡為款議，以信五年成功之說。

translations.literal: By the eighth month of the third year, Shi again memorialized, saying: "Longxi advocated Chonghuan's execution of the general that brought troops [disaster], and initiated peace talks, to confirm the claim of success within five years.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the third year, Shi Fu memorialized again: "Longxi backed Chonghuan's killing of the general that brought disaster to the army, promoted peace negotiations with the enemy, and lent credence to the boast that Liaodong would be recovered within five years.

sentences.zh: 賣國欺君，其罪莫逭。

translations.literal: Selling the country and deceiving the ruler—his crimes cannot be escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In betraying the realm and deceiving the throne, his crimes brooked no mercy.

sentences.zh: 龍錫出都，以崇煥所畀重賄數萬，轉寄姻家，巧為營幹，致國法不伸。

translations.literal: After Longxi left the capital, he took heavy bribes of tens of thousands given by Chonghuan, forwarded them through marriage connections, ingeniously worked behind the scenes, and caused the law of the state not to be enforced.
translations.idiomatic: After Longxi left the capital, he took the tens of thousands in heavy bribes Chonghuan had given him, parked them with in-laws, maneuvered craftily behind the scenes, and saw to it that justice was not done.

sentences.zh: 」帝怒，敕刑官五日內具獄。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was enraged and ordered the judicial officials to complete the case within five days.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was enraged and ordered the judicial officials to close the case within five days.

sentences.zh: 於是錦衣劉僑上崇煥獄詞。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Qiao of the Embroidered Uniform Guard submitted Chonghuan's case record.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Liu Qiao of the Embroidered Uniform Guard submitted the record of Chonghuan's case.

sentences.zh: 帝召諸臣於平臺，置崇煥重辟。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned the ministers at the Platform and imposed capital punishment on Chonghuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned the ministers to the Platform and condemned Chonghuan to death.

sentences.zh: 責龍錫私結邊臣，蒙隱不舉，令廷臣議罪。

translations.literal: He charged Longxi with privately befriending frontier officials, concealing and not reporting [crimes], and ordered the court ministers to deliberate on his punishment.
translations.idiomatic: He charged Longxi with secretly cultivating ties to border commanders and covering up what should have been exposed, and ordered the court to deliberate his sentence.

sentences.zh: 是日，群議於中府，謂：「斬帥雖龍錫啟端，而兩書有『處置慎重』語，意不在擅殺，殺文龍乃崇煥過舉。

translations.literal: That day the group deliberated in the inner yamen, saying: "Although Longxi initiated the killing of the general, both letters contain the phrase 'handle with caution,' showing the intent was not unauthorized killing; killing Wenlong was Chonghuan's excessive act.
translations.idiomatic: That day the ministers assembled in the inner yamen and judged: "Although Longxi opened the way for the general's execution, both letters contain the phrase 'handle with caution'—the intent was not to authorize murder at will. Killing Wenlong was Chonghuan's overreach.

sentences.zh: 至講款，倡自崇煥，龍錫始答以『酌量』，繼答以『天子神武，不宜講款』。

translations.literal: As for peace talks, the initiative came from Chonghuan; Longxi first replied 'weigh carefully,' then replied 'the Son of Heaven is divinely martial—peace talks are not appropriate.'
translations.idiomatic: As for negotiating peace, the initiative came from Chonghuan; Longxi first answered 'weigh the matter carefully,' then 'the Son of Heaven is divinely martial—peace talks are out of the question.'

sentences.zh: 然軍國大事，私自商度，不抗疏發奸，何所逃罪？

translations.literal: Yet on great affairs of army and state, to privately discuss and deliberate without memorializing to expose the villainy—how can guilt be escaped?
translations.idiomatic: Yet on matters of war and state, to discuss them in private correspondence without memorializing to expose the wrongdoing—what guilt could he escape?

sentences.zh: 」帝遂遣使逮之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor then sent envoys to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor then sent envoys to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 十二月逮至，下獄。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was arrested and brought in, and imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: Arrested and brought in during the twelfth month, he was cast into prison.

sentences.zh: 復疏辯，悉封上崇煥原書及所答書，帝不省。

translations.literal: He again memorialized in defense, sealing and submitting all of Chonghuan's original letters and his replies; the Emperor paid no heed.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized again in his defense, submitting Chonghuan's original letters and his own replies in full, but the Emperor would not look into them.

sentences.zh: 時群小麗名逆案者，聚謀指崇煥為逆首，龍錫等為逆黨。

translations.literal: At the time petty men who beautified their names through treason cases gathered to plot, pointing to Chonghuan as the ringleader of treason and Longxi and others as his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men who had built their reputations on treason prosecutions now met to plot, naming Chonghuan the ringleader of rebellion and Longxi and his associates accomplices.

sentences.zh: 更立一逆案相抵。

translations.literal: They further established another treason case to counterbalance it.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed an additional treason case to offset it.

sentences.zh: 謀既定，欲自兵部發之，尚書梁廷棟憚帝英明，不敢任而止。

translations.literal: Once the plot was set, they wished to launch it from the Ministry of War; Minister Liang Tingdong feared the Emperor's keen judgment, dared not take responsibility, and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Once the plot was fixed, they meant to launch it through the Ministry of War, but Minister Liang Tingdong, fearing the Emperor's sharp judgment, did not dare take responsibility and let the matter drop.

sentences.zh: 乃議龍錫大辟，且用夏言故事，設廠西市以待。

translations.literal: They then deliberated capital punishment for Longxi, and following the precedent of Xia Yan, set up the West Market of the Depot for the execution.
translations.idiomatic: They then voted for Longxi's execution and, following the precedent of Xia Yan, prepared the West Market at the Eastern Depot for his death.

sentences.zh: 帝以龍錫無逆謀，令長系。

translations.literal: The Emperor, considering that Longxi had no treasonous plot, ordered long-term imprisonment.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor judged that Longxi had no part in treason and ordered him held indefinitely.

sentences.zh: 四年正月，右中允黃道周疏言龍錫不宜坐死罪。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year, Right Middle Attendant Huang Daozhou memorialized that Longxi should not be convicted of a capital crime.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year, Huang Daozhou, Right Middle Attendant, memorialized that Longxi did not deserve the death penalty.

sentences.zh: 忤旨，貶秩調外，而帝意浸解矣。

translations.literal: Counter to the imperial will, he was demoted in rank and transferred outside; yet the Emperor's mind gradually eased.
translations.idiomatic: Defying the throne, he was demoted and posted away—yet the Emperor's anger toward Longxi slowly abated.

sentences.zh: 夏五月大旱，刑部尚書胡應臺等乞宥龍錫，給事中劉斯來繼言之，詔所司再讞。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of summer there was great drought; Minister of Justice Hu Yingtai and others begged pardon for Longxi, Supervising Secretary Liu Silai followed with the same plea, and an edict ordered the relevant office to review the case again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of summer a great drought struck; Minister of Justice Hu Yingtai and others pleaded for Longxi's pardon, and Supervising Secretary Liu Silai added his voice; the throne ordered a rehearing.

sentences.zh: 乃釋獄，戍定海衛。

translations.literal: He was then released from prison and banished to garrison at Dinghai Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Longxi was released from prison and banished to serve at Dinghai garrison.

sentences.zh: 在戍十二年，兩遇赦不原。

translations.literal: During twelve years at the garrison, he twice encountered amnesties but was not pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Through twelve years of exile he twice missed general amnesties.

sentences.zh: 其子請輸粟贖罪，會周延儒再當國，尼不行。

translations.literal: His son requested to redeem the crime by paying grain; just as Zhou Yanru again held power, [the request] was obstructed and did not proceed.
translations.idiomatic: His son offered grain to redeem his sentence, but Zhou Yanru had again taken power and blocked it.

sentences.zh: 福王時，復官歸裏。

translations.literal: During the Prince of Fu's regime, his office was restored and he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was restored to office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年六十有八。

translations.literal: Before long he died, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after, at sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 錢士升，字抑之，嘉善人。

translations.literal: Qian Shisheng, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Jiashan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Shisheng, styled Yizhi, was from Jiashan.

sentences.zh: 萬歷四十四年殿試第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: In the forty-fourth year of Wanli he ranked first in the palace examination and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He topped the palace examination in the forty-fourth year of Wanli and was appointed Hanlin Compiler.

sentences.zh: 天啟初，以養母乞歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianqi, he begged leave to return home to care for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianqi reign he retired to care for his mother.

sentences.zh: 久之，進左中允，不赴。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was promoted to Left Middle Assistant but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: Later promoted to Left Middle Assistant, he declined to serve.

sentences.zh: 高邑趙南星、同里魏大中受珰禍，及江西同年生萬燝杖死追贓，皆力為營護，破產助之，以是為東林所推。

translations.literal: Zhao Nanxing of Gaoyi and his townsman Wei Dazhong suffered disaster from the eunuch faction; and his fellow graduate of the same year Wan Zuan of Jiangxi was beaten to death while pursued for restitution—all he vigorously protected, ruining his estate to aid them, and thereby was promoted by the Donglin faction.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Nanxing of Gaoyi and his townsman Wei Dazhong fell victim to the eunuch faction, and when his Jiangxi classmate Wan Zuan was beaten to death in pursuit of restitution, he threw himself into their defense at the cost of his fortune—and won the Donglin faction's esteem.

sentences.zh: 帝操切，溫體仁以刻薄佐之，上下囂然。

translations.literal: The Emperor was demanding and sharp; Wen Tiren assisted him with harsh severity, and above and below there was uproar.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ruled with harsh exactitude; Wen Tiren abetted him with pitiless severity, and the court was in an uproar.

sentences.zh: 士升因撰《四箴》以獻，大指謂寬以禦眾，簡以臨下，虛以宅心，平以出政，其言深中時病。

translations.literal: Shisheng therefore composed the "Four Admonitions" and presented them, their main purport being: use generosity to govern the multitude, simplicity to face subordinates, emptiness to settle the mind, and evenness to carry out policy—the words deeply struck the illness of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng wrote the "Four Admonitions" and submitted them: rule the people with magnanimity, lead subordinates with restraint, keep the heart uncluttered, and govern with even hand. His words struck deep at the maladies of the age.

sentences.zh: 帝雖優旨報聞，意殊不懌也。

translations.literal: Although the Emperor replied with gracious wording acknowledging receipt, he was quite displeased in mind.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor acknowledged the memorial graciously on paper but was far from pleased.

sentences.zh: 無何，武生李琎請括江南富戶，報名輸官，行首實籍沒之法。

translations.literal: Before long, military licentiate Li Jin requested to register wealthy households in Jiangnan, have them declare their names and pay to the state, and implement the method of listing names and confiscating property.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the military licentiate Li Jin proposed registering Jiangnan's wealthy households, forcing them to declare themselves and pay up, and confiscating their property by name and deed.

sentences.zh: 士升惡之，擬旨下刑部提問，帝不許，同官溫體仁遂改輕擬。

translations.literal: Shisheng detested this, drafted a rescript to send the matter to the Ministry of Justice for interrogation; the Emperor disapproved, and his colleague Wen Tiren then revised the draft to lighter wording.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng loathed the proposal and drafted a rescript referring Li to the Ministry of Justice for interrogation; the Emperor refused, and his colleague Wen Tiren softened the draft.

sentences.zh: 士升曰：「此亂本也，當以去就爭之。

translations.literal: Shisheng said: "This is the root of disorder; one must contest it by risking one's position.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng said, "This is the seed of rebellion. I must fight it with my office.

sentences.zh: 」乃疏言：「自陳啟新言事，擢置省闥。

translations.literal: " He then memorialized, saying: "Since Chen Qixin spoke on affairs of state and was elevated to the inner cabinet,
translations.idiomatic: " He memorialized: "Since Chen Qixin's memorializing won him a place in the inner cabinet,

sentences.zh: 比來借端幸進者，實繁有徒，然未有誕肆如琎者也。

translations.literal: of late those who seized pretexts to advance by fortune have indeed been many, yet none has been so wild and unrestrained as Jin.
translations.idiomatic: men who seize any pretext to climb have been many of late, but none so reckless as Jin.

sentences.zh: 其曰縉紳豪右之家，大者千百萬，中者百十萬，以萬計者不能枚舉。

translations.literal: He says that among gentry and powerful families, the great ones [hold] millions, the middling ones hundreds of thousands, and those counted in tens of thousands cannot be enumerated.
translations.idiomatic: He claims that among gentry and magnates the greatest hold millions, the middling hundreds of thousands, and households worth ten thousand taels are beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 臣不知其所指何地。

translations.literal: Your subject does not know what place he is referring to.
translations.idiomatic: I do not know what region he has in mind.

sentences.zh: 就江南論之，富家數畝以對，百計者什六七，千計者什三四，萬計者千百中一二耳。

translations.literal: Taking Jiangnan alone, wealthy families counted by mu in response—seven or eight out of ten in the hundreds, three or four out of ten in the thousands, only one or two in a thousand or hundred among those in the ten thousands.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangnan alone, if one reckons wealth by land holdings, seven or eight in ten wealthy families count their fortunes in the hundreds, three or four in ten in the thousands, and only one or two in a thousand reach ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 江南如此，何況他省。

translations.literal: If Jiangnan is thus, how much more so other provinces.
translations.idiomatic: If this is true of Jiangnan, what of the other provinces?

sentences.zh: 且郡邑有富家，固貧民衣食之源也。

translations.literal: Moreover, when counties and districts have wealthy families, they are indeed the source of food and clothing for the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, wealthy families in the counties are the very source of livelihood for the poor.

sentences.zh: 地方水旱，有司令出錢粟，均糶濟饑，一遇寇警，令助城堡守禦，富家未嘗無益於國。

translations.literal: When locales suffer flood or drought, officials order them to supply money and grain, equally selling grain to relieve famine; when bandit alarms arise, they are ordered to aid in fortifying and defending cities—wealthy families have never been without benefit to the state.
translations.idiomatic: In flood or drought, magistrates call on them for grain and cash to sell at fair rates and feed the hungry; at the first alarm of raiders, they are summoned to help man the walls. The wealthy have never ceased to serve the realm.

sentences.zh: 《周禮》荒政十二，保富居一。

translations.literal: The "Rites of Zhou" lists twelve famine policies, and protecting the wealthy ranks first.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou list twelve famine policies, and protecting the wealthy comes first.

sentences.zh: 今以兵荒歸罪於富家朘削，議括其財而籍沒之，此秦皇不行於巴清、漢武不行於卜式者，而欲行聖明之世乎？

translations.literal: Now, attributing war and famine to the wealthy and seeking to pare them down, deliberating to seize their wealth and confiscate by registry—this is what Qin Shihuang did not impose on Ba Qing and Han Wudi did not impose on Bu Shi—yet one wishes to enact it in an era of sagely brilliance?
translations.idiomatic: To blame war and famine on the rich, strip them bare, seize their wealth and confiscate their estates—measures Qin Shihuang would not have imposed on Ba Qing, nor Han Wudi on Bu Shi—is this what we propose for an age of enlightened rule?

sentences.zh: 今秦、晉、楚、豫已無寧宇，獨江南數郡稍安。

translations.literal: Now Qin, Jin, Chu, and Yu have no peaceful territory; only several commanderies of Jiangnan are somewhat secure.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi, Shanxi, Huguang, and Henan have known no peace; only a few prefectures of Jiangnan remain calm.

sentences.zh: 此議一倡，無賴亡命相率而與富家為難，不驅天下之民胥為流寇不止。

translations.literal: Once this proposal is raised, ruffians and desperate men will successively take it up to make trouble for wealthy families, and before long will drive all the people under heaven to become roving bandits without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Let this proposal gain a hearing and ruffians and desperadoes will flock to make war on the wealthy—not long before the whole empire turns to brigandage without end.

sentences.zh: 或疑此輩乃流寇心腹，倡橫議以搖人心，豈直借端幸進已哉！

translations.literal: One may suspect these people are the heart-and-gut of the roving bandits, advocating reckless talk to shake the people's hearts—is it merely seizing a pretext for fortune to advance!
translations.idiomatic: One might suspect these men are the agents of the bandits themselves, peddling reckless schemes to shake public confidence—is this not far more than mere careerism!

sentences.zh: 」疏入，而琎已下法司提問。

translations.literal: " When the memorial arrived, Jin had already been sent down to the judicial offices for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: " By the time the memorial arrived, Jin had already been sent to the judicial offices for interrogation.

sentences.zh: 帝報曰：「即欲沽名，前疏已足致之，毋庸汲汲。

translations.literal: The Emperor replied: "If one wishes to buy a name, the previous memorial was already sufficient to achieve it—there is no need to be so eager.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor replied, "If you mean to burnish your reputation, your last memorial was fame enough—there is no need for such zeal.

sentences.zh: 」前疏謂《四箴》也。

translations.literal: " The previous memorial refers to the "Four Admonitions."
translations.idiomatic: " The "previous memorial" meant the "Four Admonitions."

sentences.zh: 士升惶懼，引罪乞休，帝即許之。

translations.literal: Shisheng was fearful and alarmed, acknowledged guilt and begged retirement; the Emperor immediately granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng, shaken, confessed fault and asked to retire; the Emperor granted his request at once.

sentences.zh: 士升初入閣，體仁頗援之。

translations.literal: When Shisheng first entered the Grand Secretariat, Tiren quite supported him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shisheng first joined the Grand Secretariat, Tiren had been a strong backer.

sentences.zh: 體仁推轂謝升、唐世濟，士升皆為助。

translations.literal: Tiren pushed forward Xie Sheng and Tang Shiji, and Shisheng assisted in all cases.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren promoted Xie Sheng and Tang Shiji, and Shisheng backed them both.

sentences.zh: 文震孟被擠，士升弗能救，論者咎之。

translations.literal: When Wen Zhenmeng was squeezed out, Shisheng could not save him; critics blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Zhenmeng was forced out, Shisheng could not shield him, and critics held it against him.

sentences.zh: 至是乃以讜言去位。

translations.literal: Only then did he leave office on account of straight counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Only now did he leave office for speaking plain truth to power.

sentences.zh: 弟士晉，萬歷中由進士除刑部主事。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shijin, in the Wanli reign through the jinshi degree, was appointed a Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shijin, a jinshi under Wanli, was appointed Principal Secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
