sentences.zh: 恤刑畿輔，平反者千百人。

translations.literal: In reviewing cases in the capital region, he overturned [wrongful convictions for] a thousand or several hundred people.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing cases in the capital region, he reversed convictions for hundreds upon hundreds.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，以山東右布政擢雲南巡撫。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign, from Right Administration Commissioner of Shandong he was promoted to Grand Coordinator of Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he rose from Right Commissioner of Shandong to Grand Coordinator of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 築師宗、新化六城，浚金針、白沙等河，平土官岑、儂兩姓之亂，頗著勞績。

translations.literal: He built six walled cities at Shizong and Xinhua, dredged the Jin Zhen, Baisha, and other rivers, pacified the disturbances of the native chieftain clans Cen and Nong, and achieved notable merit.
translations.idiomatic: He built six fortifications at Shizong and Xinhua, dredged the Jin Zhen, Baisha, and other rivers, and quelled rebellions among the native chieftains of the Cen and Nong clans, earning substantial credit.

sentences.zh: 已而經歷吳鯤化訐其營賄，體仁即擬嚴旨，且屬同官林釬弗泄，欲因弟以逐其兄。

translations.literal: Before long Administrative Assistant Wu Kunhua impeached him for soliciting bribes; Tiren immediately drafted a severe rescript, and moreover instructed colleague Lin Qian not to leak it, wishing through the younger brother to drive out the elder.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Administrative Assistant Wu Kunhua accused him of bribery; Tiren drafted a harsh edict at once and told his colleague Lin Qian to keep silent, planning to use the brother to destroy the elder Shisheng.

sentences.zh: 命下，而士晉已卒，事乃已。

translations.literal: When the order was issued, Shijin had already died, and the matter then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the order went out, Shijin was already dead, and the affair ended there.

sentences.zh: 士升，國變後七年乃卒。

translations.literal: Shisheng died only seven years after the fall of the dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng died seven years after the dynastic collapse.

sentences.zh: 成基命，字靖之，大名人，後避宣宗諱，以字行。

translations.literal: Cheng Jiming, courtesy name Jingzhi, was a native of Daming; later, to avoid the taboo of Xuanzong, he went by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Jiming, styled Jingzhi, was from Daming; later, to avoid the taboo name of the Xuanzong Emperor, he was known by his style.

sentences.zh: 萬歷三十五年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the thirty-fifth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，歷司經局洗馬，署國子監司業事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Probationer, served as Lecturer in the Directorate of Education, and acted as Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Made a Hanlin probationer, he served as Lecturer in the Directorate of Education and acting Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，疏請幸學不先白政府，執政者不悅，令以原官還局，遂請告歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, he memorialized requesting an imperial visit to the academy without first informing the chief ministers; the ruling officials were displeased, ordered him to return to his original post in the bureau, and he then requested leave to go home.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi's first year he memorialized for an imperial academy visit without clearing it with the chief ministers first; the ruling cabinet took offense, sent him back to his original post in the bureau, and he retired.

sentences.zh: 尋起少詹事。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 累官禮部右侍郎兼太子賓客，改掌南京翰林院事。

translations.literal: By accumulated appointments he reached Right Vice Minister of Rites and Companion to the Heir Apparent, then was transferred to direct the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Right Vice Minister of Rites and Companion to the Heir Apparent, then was shifted to head the Nanjing Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 六年，魏忠賢以基命為楊漣同門生，落職閑住。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Wei Zhongxian, because Jiming was a fellow student of Yang Lian, stripped him of office and ordered idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Wei Zhongxian, noting that Jiming had studied under the same teacher as Yang Lian, stripped him of office and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起吏部左侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, he was recalled as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen's first year he was recalled as Left Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 明年十月，京師戒嚴，基命請召還舊輔孫承宗，省一切浮議，仿嘉靖朝故事，增設樞臣，帝並可之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the following year, when the capital was under martial law, Jiming requested recall of the former Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong, reduction of all idle talk, following the precedent of the Jiajing reign to add military strategist ministers—the Emperor approved all.
translations.idiomatic: The following tenth month, with the capital under martial law, Jiming urged recall of former Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong, an end to empty quarrels, and new military strategist posts as in the Jiajing reign; the Emperor approved all.

sentences.zh: 逾月，拜禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，入閣輔政。

translations.literal: After more than a month, he was appointed Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the Grand Secretariat to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made Minister of Rites and Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the cabinet as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 庶吉士金聲薦僧申甫為將。

translations.literal: Hanlin Probationer Jin Sheng recommended the monk Shen Fu as general.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin probationer Jin Sheng recommended the monk Shen Fu for command.

sentences.zh: 帝令基命閱其所部兵，極言不可用，後果一戰而敗。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Jiming to inspect the troops under his command; he strongly said they could not be used, and afterward they indeed lost in a single battle.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had Jiming inspect his troops; Jiming declared them utterly useless, and they were indeed routed at the first engagement.

sentences.zh: 袁崇煥、祖大壽入衛，帝召見平臺，執崇煥屬吏，大壽在旁股栗。

translations.literal: Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou entered to guard the capital; the Emperor summoned them for audience at the Platform, handed Chonghuan over to the legal officers, and Dashou trembled in the leg at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Chonghuan and Zu Dashou arrived to defend the capital; summoned to the Platform, Chonghuan was handed to the legal officers while Dashou shook at his side.

sentences.zh: 基命獨叩頭請慎重者再，帝曰：「慎重即因循，何益？

translations.literal: Jiming alone kowtowed twice requesting caution; the Emperor said: "Caution is just procrastination—what good is it?
translations.idiomatic: Jiming alone kowtowed twice for caution. The Emperor said, "Caution is only foot-dragging—what good does it do?

sentences.zh: 」基命復叩頭曰：「敵在城下，非他時比。

translations.literal: " Jiming kowtowed again and said: "The enemy is below the walls—this is not like other times.
translations.idiomatic: " Jiming kowtowed again. "The enemy is at the gates—this is not like other times.

sentences.zh: 」帝終不省。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ultimately would not understand.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor would not heed him.

sentences.zh: 大壽至軍，即擁眾東潰，帝憂之甚。

translations.literal: When Dashou reached the army, he immediately gathered the multitude and fled east in collapse; the Emperor was deeply worried.
translations.idiomatic: Dashou reached his command and at once led his troops in a rout to the east; the Emperor was deeply alarmed.

sentences.zh: 基命曰：「令崇煥作手劄招之，當歸命也。

translations.literal: Jiming said: "Order Chonghuan to write a personal letter to summon him—he will return to his duty.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming said, "Have Chonghuan write him a personal letter of summons—he will come back.

sentences.zh: 」時兵事孔棘，基命數建白，皆允行。

translations.literal: " At the time military affairs were extremely pressing; Jiming repeatedly offered proposals, all approved and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " Military affairs were desperate; Jiming's repeated proposals were all approved and implemented.

sentences.zh: 及戒嚴，召對文華殿，帝言法紀廢弛，宜力振刷。

translations.literal: When martial law was proclaimed, summoned for audience in the Wenhua Hall, the Emperor spoke of law and discipline being lax and decayed, and that forceful renewal was appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: During the martial-law crisis, called to audience in the Wenhua Hall, the Emperor declared that law and discipline had collapsed and must be restored by force.

sentences.zh: 基命曰：「治道去太甚，譬理亂絲，當覓其緒，驟紛更益擾亂。

translations.literal: Jiming said: "In the way of governance, remove excesses; it is like sorting tangled silk—one must find the thread; sudden wholesale changes only increase disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming said, "Good government trims excess. It is like untangling silk—find the thread and pull gently; sudden wholesale changes only make the knot worse.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「慢則糾之以猛，何謂紛更？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "When lax, correct with severity—what do you mean by wholesale changes?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "When men grow slack, whip them to attention—what 'wholesale changes' do you mean?

sentences.zh: 」其後溫體仁益導帝以操切，天下遂大亂。

translations.literal: " Afterward Wen Tiren increasingly guided the Emperor toward harsh exactitude, and the realm then fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereafter Wen Tiren steered the Emperor toward ever-harsher rule, and the empire slid into chaos.

sentences.zh: 三年二月，工部主事李逢申劾基命欲脫袁崇煥罪，故乞慎重。

translations.literal: In the second month of the third year, Principal Secretary of Works Li Fengshen impeached Jiming for wishing to exonerate Yuan Chonghuan from guilt, and therefore begging for caution.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the third year, Li Fengshen of the Ministry of Works impeached Jiming for seeking to spare Yuan Chonghuan and therefore pleading for caution.

sentences.zh: 基命求罷，帝為貶逢申一秩。

translations.literal: Jiming requested dismissal; the Emperor for his sake demoted Fengshen one rank.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming offered to resign; the Emperor demoted Fengshen one rank in Jiming's defense.

sentences.zh: 韓爌、李標相繼去，基命遂為首輔，與周延儒、何如寵、錢象坤共事。

translations.literal: Han Kuang and Li Biao left in succession; Jiming then became chief Grand Secretary, serving together with Zhou Yanru, He Ruchong, and Qian Xiangkun.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Kuang and Li Biao left in turn, Jiming became chief Grand Secretary, serving alongside Zhou Yanru, He Ruchong, and Qian Xiangkun.

sentences.zh: 以恢復永平敘功，並加太子太保，進文淵閣。

translations.literal: For merit in recovering Yongping, he was jointly granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and advanced to the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Credited for the recovery of Yongping, he was made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to Grand Secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 至六月，溫體仁、吳宗達入，延儒、體仁最為帝所眷，比而傾基命，基命遂不安其位矣。

translations.literal: By the sixth month, Wen Tiren and Wu Zongda entered [the cabinet]; Yanru and Tiren were most favored by the Emperor, and joining forces they overturned Jiming—Jiming then could not rest secure in his post.
translations.idiomatic: By the sixth month Wen Tiren and Wu Zongda had joined the cabinet; Yanru and Tiren, the Emperor's favorites, worked together to undermine Jiming, who could no longer hold his ground.

sentences.zh: 方崇煥之議罪也，基命病足不入直。

translations.literal: Just when Chonghuan's guilt was being deliberated, Jiming was ill in the foot and did not attend regular duty.
translations.idiomatic: While Chonghuan's sentence was being debated, Jiming, laid up with a foot ailment, did not attend cabinet duty.

sentences.zh: 錦衣張道浚以委卸劾之，工部主事陸澄源疏繼上。

translations.literal: Zhang Daojun of the Embroidered Uniform Guard impeached him for shirking responsibility; Principal Secretary of Works Lu Chengyuan followed with a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Daojun of the Embroidered Uniform Guard impeached him for dereliction of duty, and Lu Chengyuan of the Ministry of Works added a memorial in turn.

sentences.zh: 基命奏辯曰：「澄源謂臣當兩首廷推，皆韓爌等欲藉以救崇煥。

translations.literal: Jiming memorialized in defense, saying: "Chengyuan says I headed two court nominations, both times so Han Kuang and the others wished to use this to save Chonghuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming submitted a memorial in his defense: "Chengyuan claims I headed court nomination twice, both times because Han Kuang and his faction meant to exploit the process to save Chonghuan.

sentences.zh: 當廷推時，崇煥方倚任，安知後日之敗，預謀救之。

translations.literal: At the time of court nomination, Chonghuan was still relied upon—how could one know of his later defeat and plot in advance to save him?
translations.idiomatic: At the time of those nominations Chonghuan was still in imperial favor; who could have foreseen his later downfall or schemed beforehand to rescue him?

sentences.zh: 其說祖逢申、道浚，不逐臣不止，乞放歸。

translations.literal: His account follows Fengshen and Daojun; unless I am driven out they will not stop; I beg to be released to go home.
translations.idiomatic: His story echoes Fengshen and Daojun, and they will not rest until I am removed; I beg leave to retire.

sentences.zh: 」帝慰留之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor comforted him and kept him.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor reassured him and kept him in office.

sentences.zh: 卒三疏自引去。

translations.literal: In the end he submitted three memorials and withdrew on his own.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually submitted three resignations and left office.

sentences.zh: 基命性寬厚，每事持大體。

translations.literal: Jiming's nature was generous and mild; in every matter he upheld the broad principle.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming was generous and even-tempered, always keeping sight of the larger picture.

sentences.zh: 先是，四城未復，兵部尚書梁廷棟銜總理馬世龍，將更置之，以撼樞輔承宗，基命力調劑，世龍卒收遵、永功。

translations.literal: Earlier, the four cities had not been recovered; Minister of War Liang Tingdong resented overall commander Ma Shilong and was about to replace him to shake the military strategist minister Chengzong; Jiming forcefully mediated, and Shilong finally achieved merit in Zunhua and Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with the four lost cities still unrestored, Minister of War Liang Tingdong resented overall commander Ma Shilong and planned to replace him to undermine Grand Secretary Sun Chengzong. Jiming worked hard to mediate, and Shilong finally retook Zunhua and Yongping.

sentences.zh: 尚書張鳳翔、喬允升、韓繼思相繼下吏，並為申理。

translations.literal: Ministers Zhang Fengxiang, Qiao Yunsheng, and Han Jisi were successively sent to the legal officers; he pleaded on behalf of all of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ministers Zhang Fengxiang, Qiao Yunsheng, and Han Jisi were sent before the courts in succession, he pleaded their cases.

sentences.zh: 副都御史易應昌下詔獄，以基命言，改下法司。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yi Yingchang was sent to the imperial prison; on Jiming's word, he was transferred to the regular judiciary.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Yi Yingchang was committed to the imperial prison, but at Jiming's urging his case was moved to the regular courts.

sentences.zh: 御史李長春、給事中杜齊芳坐私書事，將置重典。

translations.literal: Censor Li Changchun and Supervising Secretary Du Qifang were implicated in a private letter affair and were about to receive heavy punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Changchun and Supervising Secretary Du Qifang were charged in a private-correspondence case and faced severe penalties.

sentences.zh: 基命力救，不聽，長跪會極門，言：「祖宗立法，真死罪猶三覆奏，豈有詔獄一訊遽置極刑？

translations.literal: Jiming strove to save them, but was not heeded; he knelt long at the Huaji Gate, saying: "Our forefathers established the law: even for true capital crimes there is still triple review—how can the imperial prison, with one interrogation, hastily impose extreme punishment?
translations.idiomatic: Jiming fought to save them in vain, then knelt at the Huaji Gate from dawn, saying, "Our ancestors' law required three reviews even for genuine capital offenses—how can the imperial prison condemn men to death after a single hearing?

sentences.zh: 」自辰至酉未起。

translations.literal: " From the hour chen to the hour you he did not rise.
translations.idiomatic: " He remained kneeling from morning until evening.

sentences.zh: 帝意解，得遣戍。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mind softened, and they were able to be sent into exile.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor relented, and they were banished instead.

sentences.zh: 逢申初劾基命，後以炮炸下獄擬戍，帝猶以為輕，亦以基命言得如擬。

translations.literal: Fengshen had originally impeached Jiming; later, for a cannon explosion he was imprisoned and sentenced to exile; the Emperor still thought it lenient, but on Jiming's word the sentence as proposed was allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Fengshen had first impeached Jiming; later he himself was imprisoned after a cannon accident and sentenced to exile. The Emperor still thought that too lenient, but at Jiming's urging the proposed sentence stood.

sentences.zh: 為首輔者數月，帝欲委政延儒，遂為其黨所逐。

translations.literal: As chief Grand Secretary for several months, the Emperor wished to entrust government to Yanru, and so he was driven out by that faction.
translations.idiomatic: He served as chief minister for only a few months; the Emperor meant to entrust power to Yanru, and Yanru's faction forced him out.

sentences.zh: 八年卒於家。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈少保，謚文穆。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian and given the posthumous title Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Junior Guardian with the title Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 何如寵，字康侯，桐城人。

translations.literal: He Ruchong, courtesy name Kanghou, was a native of Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He Ruchong, styled Kanghou, was from Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 父思鰲，知棲霞縣，有德於民。

translations.literal: His father Si'ao was magistrate of Qixia County and had virtue toward the people.
translations.idiomatic: His father Si'ao served as magistrate of Qixia County and was beloved by the people.

sentences.zh: 如寵登萬歷二十六年進士，由庶吉士累遷國子監祭酒。

translations.literal: Ruchong became a jinshi in the twenty-sixth year of Wanli; from Hanlin Probationer he was promoted by stages to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchong took his jinshi in Wanli 26, rose from Hanlin probationer to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，官禮部右侍郎，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign, he held office as Right Vice Minister of Rites and assisted in directing the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi he served as Right Vice Minister of Rites and helped administer the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，廷推左侍郎，魏廣微言如寵與左光鬥同里友善，遂奪職閑住。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, at court nomination for Left Vice Minister, Wei Guangwei said Ruchong was friendly with Zuo Guangdou as fellow townsmen, and so his post was stripped and he was ordered to idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, when the Left Vice Minister was nominated at court, Wei Guangwei charged that Ruchong was on friendly terms with his fellow townsman Zuo Guangdou; Ruchong was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，起為吏部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen's first year he was recalled as Right Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 未至，拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Before he arrived, he was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before he even arrived, he was appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 宗藩婚嫁命名，例請於朝。

translations.literal: For marriage, naming, and other affairs of the imperial clans, by precedent permission was requested from the court.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen were required by precedent to seek court permission for marriages and the naming of children.

sentences.zh: 貧者為部所稽，自萬歷末至是，積疏累千，有白首不能完家室，骨朽而尚未名者。

translations.literal: The poor were held up by the ministry; from the end of Wanli to this time, accumulated petitions numbered in the thousands—some grew white-haired unable to complete their household, bones decayed yet still unnamed.
translations.idiomatic: Poor clansmen were stalled by the ministry; from late Wanli onward petitions piled up by the thousand. Some grew old unable to marry, others died unnamed.

sentences.zh: 用如寵請，貧宗得嫁娶者六百余人。

translations.literal: On adopting Ruchong's request, more than six hundred poor clansmen obtained marriage.
translations.idiomatic: At Ruchong's urging, more than six hundred impoverished clansmen were allowed to marry.

sentences.zh: 大學士劉鴻訓以增敕事，帝怒不測，如寵力為剖析，得免死戍邊。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun, over the matter of adding imperial edicts, aroused the Emperor's unpredictable anger; Ruchong forcefully analyzed it for him, and he escaped death and was exiled to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Liu Hongxun provoked the Emperor's wrath over unauthorized edicts; Ruchong argued his case forcefully, and Liu escaped execution and was banished to the border.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，京師戒嚴，都人桀黠者，請以私財聚眾助官軍，朝議壯之。

translations.literal: The next winter the capital was under martial law; sharp and cunning men of the capital requested to gather crowds with private funds to assist the official army—the court debate found this bold.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter, with the capital under martial law, enterprising townsfolk proposed raising private funds and crowds to aid the army; many at court applauded the idea.

sentences.zh: 如寵力言其叵測，不善用，必啟內釁。

translations.literal: Ruchong forcefully said its unpredictability made it ill to employ—it would surely open internal strife.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchong strongly warned that such schemes were unpredictable and dangerous, and would surely spark internal unrest.

sentences.zh: 帝召問，對如初。

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned and questioned him; he answered as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor summoned him and questioned him; he gave the same answer.

sentences.zh: 帝出片紙示之，則得之偵事，與如寵言合，由是受知。

translations.literal: The Emperor produced a slip of paper to show him—it contained intelligence obtained that accorded with Ruchong's words, and thereby he gained the Emperor's trust.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor showed him a slip of intercepted intelligence that bore out Ruchong's warning, and from then on Ruchong won the Emperor's confidence.

sentences.zh: 十二月，命與周延儒、錢象坤俱以本官兼東閣大學士，入閣輔政。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he was ordered, together with Zhou Yanru and Qian Xiangkun, each to retain his original rank while also serving as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the Grand Secretariat to assist in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he was appointed, along with Zhou Yanru and Qian Xiangkun, Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion while retaining his existing posts, and entered the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 帝欲族袁崇煥，以如寵申救，免死者三百余口。

translations.literal: The Emperor wished to exterminate Yuan Chonghuan's clan; on Ruchong's intercession more than three hundred lives were spared death.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor sought to exterminate Yuan Chonghuan's entire clan, Ruchong's appeal spared more than three hundred lives.

sentences.zh: 累加少保、戶部尚書、武英殿大學士。

translations.literal: By accumulated promotion he was made Junior Guardian, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively made Junior Guardian, Minister of Revenue, and Grand Secretary of the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 四年春，副延儒總裁會試。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year he assisted Yanru in chief compilation of the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year he assisted Yanru in overseeing the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 事竣，即乞休，疏九上乃允。

translations.literal: When the affair was finished, he immediately requested retirement; after nine memorials it was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Once the examination was done, he immediately sought retirement; only after nine memorials was he allowed to leave.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，陳惇大明作之道。

translations.literal: At farewell audience he set forth the Way of honoring sincere accomplishment of the Great Bright.
translations.idiomatic: Taking leave of the throne, he expounded the Way of earnestly upholding the Ming dynasty.

sentences.zh: 抵家，復請時觀《通鑒》，察古今理亂忠佞，語甚切。

translations.literal: On reaching home, he again requested that [the Emperor] from time to time read the Comprehensive Mirror, examining loyalty and treachery and order and disorder through the ages—the words were very earnest.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he wrote again, urging the Emperor to read the Comprehensive Mirror regularly and weigh loyalty against treachery across history; his words were urgent and sincere.

sentences.zh: 六年，延儒罷政，體仁當為首輔。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Yanru was removed from government; Tiren ought to become chief Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Yanru left office, and Tiren was slated to become chief minister.

sentences.zh: 而延儒憾體仁排己，謀起如寵以抑之，如寵畏體仁，六疏辭，體仁遂為首輔。

translations.literal: But Yanru resented Tiren for having pushed him out and plotted to recall Ruchong to check him; Ruchong feared Tiren and submitted six memorials declining; Tiren then became chief Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru, resenting Tiren for forcing him out, plotted to recall Ruchong to counter him; Ruchong, afraid of Tiren, declined six times, and Tiren became chief minister.

sentences.zh: 如寵性孝友。

translations.literal: Ruchong's nature was filial and brotherly.
translations.idiomatic: Ruchong was deeply filial and devoted to his kin.

sentences.zh: 母年九十，色養不衰。

translations.literal: His mother was ninety years old; his cheerful nurture did not decline.
translations.idiomatic: His mother lived to ninety, and he cared for her with undiminished devotion.

sentences.zh: 操行恬雅，與物無競，難進易退，世尤高之。

translations.literal: His conduct was calm and refined, without contention with others; hard to advance yet easy to withdraw—the age especially honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle and uncontentious, reluctant to seek office yet quick to leave it, he was especially admired by his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 十四年卒。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourteenth year.

sentences.zh: 福王時，贈太保，謚文端。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted Grand Guardian and given the posthumous title Wenduan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the title Wenduan.

sentences.zh: 兄如申，與如寵同舉進士。

translations.literal: His elder brother Rushen, together with Ruchong, passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Rushen passed the jinshi examination in the same year as Ruchong.

sentences.zh: 官戶部郎中，督餉遼東。

translations.literal: He served as Director in the Ministry of Revenue, supervising grain transport in Liaodong.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a director in the Ministry of Revenue, overseeing grain supplies in Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 有清操，軍士請復留二載。

translations.literal: He had pure integrity; the soldiers requested that he be kept another two years.
translations.idiomatic: Known for his integrity, the troops asked that he be kept on for another two years.

sentences.zh: 終浙江右布政使。

translations.literal: He ended as Right Provincial Administration Commissioner of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Right Provincial Commissioner of Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 錢象坤，字弘載，會稽人。

translations.literal: Qian Xiangkun, courtesy name Hongzai, was a native of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiangkun, styled Hongzai, was from Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: He became a jinshi in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the twenty-ninth year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討，進諭德，轉庶子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Hanlin Probationer, appointed Reviser, advanced to Preceptor, and transferred to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: Made a Hanlin probationer, he served as Reviser, rose to Preceptor, and became Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 泰昌改元，官少詹事，直講筵。

translations.literal: When Taichang changed the era name, he held office as Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and attended the lecture hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Taichang reign he was made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and lectured before the throne.

sentences.zh: 講畢，見中官王安與執政議事，即趨出。

translations.literal: When the lecture finished, he saw the eunuch Wang An discussing affairs with the ruling ministers and immediately hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: After lecturing he saw the eunuch Wang An consulting with the chief ministers and immediately withdrew.

sentences.zh: 安使人延之，堅不入。

translations.literal: An sent someone to invite him in; he firmly would not enter.
translations.idiomatic: Wang An sent someone to fetch him, but he steadfastly refused to join them.

sentences.zh: 天啟中，給事中論織造，語侵中貴，詔予杖，閣臣救不得。

translations.literal: In the Tianqi reign, a Supervising Secretary discussed silk weaving; his words infringed on the senior eunuchs—the Emperor ordered beating with rods; Grand Secretaries could not save him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Tianqi a supervising secretary criticized imperial silk production in terms that offended senior eunuchs; the Emperor ordered him beaten, and the Grand Secretaries could not intervene.

sentences.zh: 象坤語葉向高講筵面奏之，乃免。

translations.literal: Xiangkun told Ye Xianggao to memorialize it face-to-face at the lecture hall, and thereby [the beating] was waived.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangkun asked Ye Xianggao to raise the matter at the lecture hall; the beating was canceled.

sentences.zh: 時行立枷法，慘甚，象坤白之帝，多所寬釋。

translations.literal: At the time the cangue law was established—it was extremely cruel; Xiangkun informed the Emperor, and many were leniently released.
translations.idiomatic: The cangue punishment had lately been imposed with terrible severity; Xiangkun appealed to the Emperor and secured the release of many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部右侍郎兼太子賓客。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Right Vice Minister of Rites and Companion to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Right Vice Minister of Rites and Companion to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四年七月，向高辭位。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the fourth year, Xianggao resigned his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of the fourth year Ye Xianggao resigned.

sentences.zh: 御史黃公輔慮象坤柄政，請留向高，詆象坤甚力。

translations.literal: Censor Huang Gongfu, fearing Xiangkun would wield government, requested that Xianggao be kept; he slandered Xiangkun with great force.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Huang Gongfu, fearing Xiangkun would dominate the government, urged that Ye Xianggao be retained and attacked Xiangkun vigorously.

sentences.zh: 象坤遂辭去。

translations.literal: Xiangkun then resigned and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangkun resigned in response.

sentences.zh: 六年，廷推南京禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was court-nominated Minister of Rites at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was nominated Minister of Rites at Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 魏忠賢私人指為繆昌期黨，落職閑住。

translations.literal: Wei Zhongxian's private man pointed to him as of Miao Changqi's faction; he was stripped of office and ordered to idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: A follower of Wei Zhongxian denounced him as an ally of Miao Changqi, and he was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，召拜禮部尚書，協理詹事府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen, he was summoned and appointed Minister of Rites, assisting in directing the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen's first year he was recalled as Minister of Rites and helped administer the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 明年冬，都城被兵，條禦敵三策。

translations.literal: The next winter the capital was attacked by troops; he set forth three strategies for resisting the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: The following winter, when enemy troops threatened the capital, he submitted three plans for defense.

sentences.zh: 奉命登陴分守，祁寒不懈。

translations.literal: Ordered to ascend the battlements to divide defense, in bitter cold he did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to the ramparts to hold a sector of the wall, he kept at his post through fierce cold without flagging.

sentences.zh: 帝覘知，遂與何如寵並相。

translations.literal: The Emperor observed and knew; then together with He Ruchong he was made Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor took note and appointed him Grand Secretary alongside He Ruchong.

sentences.zh: 明年，溫體仁入，象坤其門生，讓而居其下。

translations.literal: The next year Wen Tiren entered; Xiangkun was his student and yielded, taking rank below him.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wen Tiren joined the cabinet; Xiangkun, his former student, deferentially ranked below him.

sentences.zh: 累加少保，進武英殿。

translations.literal: By accumulated promotion he was made Junior Guardian and advanced to the Wuying Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was successively made Junior Guardian and promoted to the Wuying Hall.

sentences.zh: 象坤在翰林，與龍錫、謙益、士升並負物望，有「四錢」之目。

translations.literal: Xiangkun in the Hanlin, together with Longxi, Qianyi, and Shisheng, all bore public esteem; there was the designation "Four Qians."
translations.idiomatic: As a Hanlin scholar Xiangkun, together with Longxi, Qianyi, and Shisheng, enjoyed great public esteem and was counted among the "Four Qians."

sentences.zh: 及體仁相，無附和跡。

translations.literal: When Tiren became Grand Secretary, there was no trace of flattery from him.
translations.idiomatic: When Tiren became chief minister, Xiangkun showed no sign of currying favor.

sentences.zh: 四年，御史水佳允連劾兵部尚書梁廷棟，廷棟不待旨即奏辯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Censor Shui Jiayun repeatedly impeached Minister of War Liang Tingdong; Tingdong, without awaiting imperial command, immediately memorialized in defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Censor Shui Jiayun repeatedly impeached Minister of War Liang Tingdong, who defended himself by memorial without waiting for the throne's directive.

sentences.zh: 廷棟故出象坤門，佳允疑象坤泄之，語侵象坤。

translations.literal: Tingdong had originally come from Xiangkun's gate; Jiayun suspected Xiangkun had leaked it, and his words infringed on Xiangkun.
translations.idiomatic: Tingdong had been Xiangkun's protégé; Jiayun suspected Xiangkun had tipped him off and turned his attack on Xiangkun.

sentences.zh: 延儒以廷棟嘗發其私人贓罪，惡之，並惡象坤。

translations.literal: Yanru, because Tingdong had once exposed the graft crimes of his private man, hated him and also hated Xiangkun.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru hated Tingdong for having once exposed corruption among his clients, and extended that hatred to Xiangkun.

sentences.zh: 象坤遂五疏引疾去，廷棟落職。

translations.literal: Xiangkun then submitted five memorials citing illness and left; Tingdong was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangkun submitted five sick-leave memorials and resigned; Tingdong was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 給事中吳執禦、傅朝佑稱象坤難進易退，不當以門生累，不聽。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretaries Wu Zhiyu and Fu Chaoyou said Xiangkun was hard to advance yet easy to withdraw and ought not be implicated because of a student; [the Emperor] did not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretaries Wu Zhiyu and Fu Chaoyou argued that Xiangkun, who was slow to seek office and quick to leave it, should not be punished for a protégé's conduct; the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 家居十年，無病而卒。

translations.literal: At home for ten years, without illness he died.
translations.idiomatic: After ten years at home he died without ever having been ill.

sentences.zh: 贈太保，謚文貞，蔭一子中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Guardian, given the posthumous title Wenzhen, and one son was granted privilege as a Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Grand Guardian with the title Wenzhen, and one son received the hereditary privilege of Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 徐光啟，字子先，上海人。

translations.literal: Xu Guangqi, courtesy name Zixian, was a native of Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guangqi, styled Zixian, was from Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十五年舉鄉試第一，又七年成進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Wanli he placed first in the provincial examination; seven years later he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He placed first in the provincial exams in Wanli 25 and took his jinshi seven years later.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士歷贊善。

translations.literal: From Hanlin Probationer he served through the post of Supporter.
translations.idiomatic: After serving as a Hanlin probationer he rose to Supporter in the Heir Apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 從西洋人利瑪竇學天文、歷算、火器，盡其術。

translations.literal: From the Western man Matteo Ricci he studied astronomy, calendrical calculation, and firearms, mastering his arts completely.
translations.idiomatic: He studied astronomy, calendrical science, and firearms with the Westerner Matteo Ricci and mastered Ricci's learning.

sentences.zh: 遂遍習兵機、屯田、鹽策、水利諸書。

translations.literal: Then he thoroughly studied books on military strategy, garrison farming, salt policy, water control, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: He went on to study military affairs, garrison agriculture, salt administration, hydraulic works, and related subjects in depth.

sentences.zh: 楊鎬四路喪師，京師大震。

translations.literal: Yang Hao lost his army on four routes; the capital was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Hao lost his armies on four fronts, the capital was convulsed with alarm.

sentences.zh: 累疏請練兵自效，神宗壯之，超擢少詹事兼河南道御史。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized requesting to drill troops and offer himself for service; Shenzong was impressed and promoted him out of turn to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent Henan Circuit Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to train troops and serve in person; the Wanli Emperor was impressed and abruptly promoted him to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent and concurrent censor of the Henan circuit.

sentences.zh: 練兵通州，列上十議。

translations.literal: He drilled troops at Tongzhou and submitted ten proposals in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: He drilled troops at Tongzhou and submitted ten reform proposals.

sentences.zh: 時遼事方急，不能如所請。

translations.literal: At the time Liaodong affairs were urgently pressing; [the court] could not do as he requested.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong was in crisis, and the court could not grant what he asked.

sentences.zh: 光啟疏爭，乃稍給以民兵戎械。

translations.literal: Guangqi memorialized disputing it, and then a little was supplied in the way of militia weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi protested by memorial, and the court finally granted him some militia arms and equipment.

sentences.zh: 未幾，熹宗即位。

translations.literal: Before long Xizong acceded.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Tianqi Emperor ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 光啟誌不得展，請裁去，不聽。

translations.literal: Guangqi's ambition could not be unfolded; he requested that the post be cut, but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to carry out his plans, Guangqi asked that his post be abolished, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 既而以疾歸。

translations.literal: Soon after he returned home on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 遼陽破，召起之。

translations.literal: When Liaoyang fell, he was summoned and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: After Liaoyang fell he was recalled to office.

sentences.zh: 還朝，力請多鑄西洋大炮，以資城守。

translations.literal: Returning to court, he forcefully requested casting many Western great cannons to support city defense.
translations.idiomatic: Back at court, he strongly urged casting large numbers of Western-style cannons for city defense.

sentences.zh: 帝善其言。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the proposal.

sentences.zh: 方議用，而光啟與兵部尚書崔景榮議不合，御史邱兆麟劾之，復移疾歸。

translations.literal: Just as it was being deliberated for use, Guangqi and Minister of War Cui Jingrong could not agree in counsel; Censor Qiu Zhaolin impeached him, and he again cited illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: While adoption was under discussion, Guangqi clashed with Minister of War Cui Jingrong; Censor Qiu Zhaolin impeached him, and he retired again on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 天啟三年起故官，旋擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianqi he was recalled to his former office and soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 3 he was restored to his former post and soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，魏忠賢黨智鋌劾之，落職閑住。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Wei Zhongxian's partisan Zhi Ting impeached him; he was stripped of office and ordered to idle residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year a follower of Wei Zhongxian named Zhi Ting impeached him, and he was stripped of office and sent home.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年召還，復申練兵之說。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned back and again set forth the doctrine of drilling troops.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled in Chongzhen's first year, he again pressed his plan for training troops.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以左侍郎理部事。

translations.literal: Before long, as Left Vice Minister he administered the ministry's affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was put in charge of the ministry as Left Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 帝憂國用不足，敕廷臣獻屯鹽善策。

translations.literal: The emperor worried that state revenue was insufficient and ordered court officials to submit good policies on military colonies and salt.
translations.idiomatic: Worried about insufficient state revenue, the Emperor ordered court officials to propose sound policies on military farming and the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 光啟言屯政在乎墾荒，鹽政在嚴禁私販。

translations.literal: Guangqi said that the colony policy lay in opening wasteland, and the salt policy lay in strictly forbidding private trafficking.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi argued that military colonies depended on reclaiming wasteland, and salt policy on strictly prohibiting illicit trade.

sentences.zh: 帝褒納之，擢本部尚書。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it, and promoted him to Minister of his own ministry.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his advice and adopted it, elevating him to Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時帝以日食失驗，欲罪臺官。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor, because a solar eclipse prediction failed, wished to punish the astronomic bureau officials.
translations.idiomatic: Around this time a predicted solar eclipse failed to match observation, and the Emperor wanted to punish the officials of the Astronomic Bureau.

sentences.zh: 光啟言：「臺官測候本郭守敬法。

translations.literal: Guangqi said: "The bureau officials' calendrical observations originally follow Guo Shoujing's methods.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi said, "The Bureau's calculations follow Guo Shoujing's methods.

sentences.zh: 元時嘗當食不食，守敬且爾，無怪臺官之失占。

translations.literal: In Yuan times there were cases when an eclipse should have occurred but did not; even Guo Shoujing was so—no wonder the bureau officials' misprediction.
translations.idiomatic: Even in Yuan times eclipses sometimes failed to appear when predicted; even Guo Shoujing's system had such errors—there is nothing surprising in the Bureau's mistake.

sentences.zh: 臣聞歷久必差，宜及時修正。

translations.literal: I have heard that calendrical systems over time inevitably drift; it is appropriate to revise them in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that calendars inevitably drift with time; they should be revised promptly.

sentences.zh: 」帝從其言，詔西洋人龍華民、鄧玉函、羅雅谷等推算歷法，光啟為監督。

translations.literal: " The emperor followed his words and ordered the Westerners Long Hua Min, Deng Yuhan, Luo Yagu and others to calculate the calendar, with Guangqi as supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed and ordered the Westerners Long Hua Min, Deng Yuhan, and Luo Yagu to work out a new calendar, with Guangqi overseeing the project.

sentences.zh: 四年春正月，光啟進《日躔歷指》一卷、《測天約說》二卷、《大測》二卷、《日躔表》二卷、《割圜八線表》六卷、《黃道升度》七卷、《黃赤距度表》一卷、《通率表》一卷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, spring, first month, Guangqi presented "Calendrical Guide to Solar Motion," one juan; "Essential Notes on Measuring Heaven," two juan; "Great Survey," two juan; "Tables of Solar Motion," two juan; "Tables of the Eight Lines for Circle Division," six juan; "Ascension of the Yellow Path," seven juan; "Tables of Ecliptic and Equatorial Distances," one juan; and "Tables of General Ratios," one juan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring in the fourth year, Guangqi submitted eight works: one juan of A Calendrical Guide to Solar Motion; two of Essential Notes on Heavenly Measurement; two of The Great Survey; two of Tables of Solar Motion; six of Tables of the Eight Lines for Circle Division; seven of Ascension along the Yellow Path; one of Tables of Ecliptic and Equatorial Distances; and one of Tables of General Ratios.

sentences.zh: 是冬十月辛丑朔日食，復上測候四說。

translations.literal: That winter, on the first day xinchou of the tenth month there was a solar eclipse; he again submitted four propositions on observation.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, on the first day of the tenth month (xinchou), a solar eclipse occurred, and he submitted four additional treatises on observation and calculation.

sentences.zh: 其辯時差裏差之法，最為詳密。

translations.literal: His method of distinguishing time difference and parallax was the most detailed and precise.
translations.idiomatic: His exposition of time difference and parallax was the most thorough and precise of all.

sentences.zh: 五年五月，以本官兼東閣大學士，入參機務，與鄭以偉並命。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, fifth month, with his present office he was additionally made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entered to participate in confidential affairs, and was appointed together with Zheng Yiwei.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fifth year he was made Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion while retaining his ministry post, entered the inner councils, and was appointed at the same time as Zheng Yiwei.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子太保，進文淵閣。

translations.literal: Soon he was additionally made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and advanced to the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon further appointed Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and promoted to the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 光啟雅負經濟才，有誌用世。

translations.literal: Guangqi had long possessed talent for statecraft and the will to serve the age.
translations.idiomatic: Guangqi had long been known for practical statesmanship and a desire to serve the realm.

sentences.zh: 及柄用，年已老，值周延儒、溫體仁專政，不能有所建白。

translations.literal: When he came to hold power, he was already old; he met Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren's monopolized government and could not set forth proposals.
translations.idiomatic: By the time he wielded real influence he was already old; with Zhou Yanru and Wen Tiren in control, he was unable to put forward any lasting reforms.

sentences.zh: 明年十月卒。

translations.literal: The next year, in the tenth month, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following tenth month.

sentences.zh: 贈少保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Junior Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Junior Guardian.

sentences.zh: 鄭以偉，字子器，上饒人。

translations.literal: Zheng Yiwei, courtesy name Ziqi, was a man of Shangrao.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yiwei, styled Ziqi, was a native of Shangrao.

sentences.zh: 萬歷二十九年進士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Wanli he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Wanli 29.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授檢討，累遷少詹事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be a bachelor, appointed reviser, and repeatedly promoted to Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Made a Hanlin bachelor, he was appointed reviser and rose step by step to Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 泰昌元年，官禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang he served as Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Taichang 1 he was Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，光宗祔廟，當祧憲宗，太常少卿洪文衡以睿宗不當入廟，請祧奉玉芝宮，以偉不可而止，論者卒是文衡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, when Emperor Guangzong was enshrined in the ancestral temple, the rites required removing Emperor Xianzong from the temple. Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Hong Wenheng argued that Emperor Ruizong should not enter the temple and requested that reverence be moved to Yuzhi Palace; Yiwei refused and it stopped; critics in the end sided with Wenheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi 1, when the late Emperor Guangzong was installed in the ancestral temple, Emperor Xianzong was to be removed to make room. Vice Director Hong Wenheng of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices argued that Emperor Ruizong ought not remain in the temple and proposed shifting his worship to Yuzhi Palace; Yiwei blocked the proposal and the matter ended—but commentators ultimately sided with Wenheng.

sentences.zh: 尋以左侍郎協理詹事府。

translations.literal: Soon as Left Vice Minister he assisted in administering the Household of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Left Vice Minister and put in charge of the Household of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 四年，以偉直講筵，與珰忤，上疏告歸。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Yiwei was upright at the lecture sessions, offended the eunuch faction, and memorialized to request leave to return.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year his blunt conduct at the imperial lectures brought him into conflict with the eunuch faction; he submitted a memorial asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen he was summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 2 he was recalled and appointed Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 久之，與光啟並相，再辭，不允。

translations.literal: After a long while, together with Guangqi he became grand secretary; he declined twice but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made grand secretary alongside Guangqi; he declined twice, but the Emperor would not accept.

sentences.zh: 以偉修潔自好，書過目不忘，文章奧博，而票擬非其所長。

translations.literal: Yiwei was upright and pure in self-regard; books he forgot nothing once seen; his writing was profound and broad, but drafting rescripts was not his strength.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwei was fastidious and morally self-disciplined; he never forgot a book once read; his essays were learned and deep—but drafting imperial rescripts was not his forte.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾富於萬卷，窘於數行，乃為後進所藐。

translations.literal: He once said: "I am rich in ten thousand juan but cramped in a few lines, and so am despised by my juniors.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "I am rich in ten thousand volumes but helpless before a few lines of draft—and so the younger officials look down on me.

sentences.zh: 」章疏中有「何況」二字，誤以為人名也，擬旨提問，帝駁改始悟。

translations.literal: " In a memorial there were the two characters "hekuang" (moreover); he mistakenly took them as a personal name, drafted a rescript summoning the person for questioning; the emperor rejected and revised it before he realized.
translations.idiomatic: In one memorial he misread the phrase "how much more so" (hekuang) as someone's name and drafted a rescript ordering that person brought in for questioning; only when the Emperor sent it back for revision did he realize his mistake.

sentences.zh: 自是詞臣為帝輕，遂有館員須歷推知之諭，而閣臣不專用翰林矣。

translations.literal: From this literary officials were lightly regarded by the emperor; thereupon came an edict that academy members must have served as magistrates, and grand secretaries no longer used Hanlin exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the literary Hanlin were held lightly by the Emperor; an edict followed that academy officials must first serve as local magistrates, and the Grand Secretariat no longer drew exclusively from the Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 以偉累乞休，不允。

translations.literal: Yiwei repeatedly begged retirement; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwei repeatedly asked to retire, but was refused each time.

sentences.zh: 明年六月，卒官，贈太子太保。

translations.literal: The next year, sixth month, he died in office and was posthumously granted Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office the following sixth month and was posthumously honored as Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 御史言光啟、以偉相繼沒，蓋棺之日，囊無余貲，請優恤以愧貪墨者。

translations.literal: A censor said Guangqi and Yiwei died in succession; the day the coffin was closed, their purses held no surplus wealth—he requested generous posthumous care to shame the greedy.
translations.idiomatic: A censor noted that Guangqi and Yiwei had died in quick succession with empty purses on the day their coffins were sealed, and asked that they be handsomely honored so as to shame the corrupt.

sentences.zh: 帝納之，乃謚光啟文定，以偉文恪。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it and posthumously titled Guangqi Wendīng and Yiwei Wenkè.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor agreed, posthumously naming Guangqi Wendīng and Yiwei Wenkè.

sentences.zh: 其後二年，同安林釬為大學士，未半歲而卒。

translations.literal: Two years later Lin Qian of Tong'an became grand secretary; before half a year he died.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Lin Qian of Tong'an was made grand secretary, but died within half a year.

sentences.zh: 亦有言其清者，得謚文穆。

translations.literal: There were also those who spoke of his integrity; he received the posthumous title Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: Reports of his integrity earned him the posthumous title Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 釬，字實甫，萬歷四十四年殿試第三人，授編修。

translations.literal: Qian, courtesy name Shifu, in the forty-fourth year of Wanli was third in the palace examination and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, styled Shifu, placed third in the palace examination of Wanli 44 and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 天啟時，任國子司業。

translations.literal: In Tianqi times he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianqi reign he served as Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 監生陸萬齡請建魏忠賢祠於太學旁，具簿醵金，強釬為倡。

translations.literal: Academy student Lu Wanling requested building a Wei Zhongxian shrine beside the Imperial Academy, prepared a register to collect money, and forced Qian to be the first donor.
translations.idiomatic: An academy student named Lu Wanling proposed building a shrine to Wei Zhongxian beside the Imperial Academy, drew up a subscription register, and tried to bully Qian into leading the contributions.

sentences.zh: 釬援筆塗抹，即夕掛冠欞星門徑歸，忠賢矯旨削其籍。

translations.literal: Qian took the brush and crossed it out; that same evening he hung his cap and left through the Star-Gathering Gate straight home; Zhongxian forged an edict stripping him of registration.
translations.idiomatic: Qian scratched out the entry, that very evening hung up his official cap at the Gathering Stars Gate and went straight home; Zhongxian forged an edict striking him from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 崇禎改元，起少詹事。

translations.literal: When Chongzhen changed the reign title, he was recalled as Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Chongzhen reign he was recalled as Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 九年由禮部侍郎入閣，有謹願誠恪之稱。

translations.literal: In the ninth year from Vice Minister of Rites he entered the Grand Secretariat; he had the reputation of being cautious, sincere, and reverent.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he entered the Grand Secretariat from the post of Vice Minister of Rites and was known for diligence, sincerity, and integrity.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝念光啟博學強識，索其家遣書。

translations.literal: After a long while the emperor remembered Guangqi's broad learning and strong memory and sought the books left by his family.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the Emperor remembered Guangqi's erudition and retentive mind and asked his family for his surviving manuscripts.

sentences.zh: 子驥入謝，進《農政全書》六十卷。

translations.literal: His son Ji entered to give thanks and presented "Complete Treatise on Agriculture," sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ji came to court to give thanks and presented the sixty-juan Complete Treatise on Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 詔令有司刊布，加贈太保，其孫為中書舍人。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the relevant offices to publish it, additionally posthumously granted Grand Guardian, and his grandson was made Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the work published, further posthumously honored Guangqi as Grand Guardian, and appointed his grandson a Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 文震孟，字文起，吳縣人，待詔征明曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wen Zhenmeng, courtesy name Wenqi, was a man of Wuxian—the great-grandson of daizhao Zhengming.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Zhenmeng, styled Wenqi, was from Wuxian and was the great-grandson of the celebrated artist Wen Zhengming.

sentences.zh: 祖國子博士彭，父衛輝同知元發，並有名行。

translations.literal: His grandfather Peng was a doctor of the Imperial Academy; his father Yuanfa was Vice Prefect of Weihui—both were known for conduct and reputation.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Peng had been a Doctor of the Imperial Academy; his father Yuanfa had served as Vice Prefect of Weihui—both men were noted for their character.

sentences.zh: 震孟弱冠以《春秋》舉於鄉，十赴會試。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng at weak crown age passed the provincial examination in the Spring and Autumn Annals; he attended the metropolitan examination ten times.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng passed the provincial examination in the Spring and Autumn Annals while still young and sat the metropolitan examination ten times.

sentences.zh: 至天啟二年，殿試第一，授修撰。

translations.literal: Reaching the second year of Tianqi, he was first in the palace examination and was appointed drafting compiler.
translations.idiomatic: At last in Tianqi 2 he came in first in the palace examination and was appointed Senior Compiler.

sentences.zh: 時魏忠賢漸用事，外廷應之，數斥逐大臣。

translations.literal: At the time Wei Zhongxian gradually wielded power; the outer court responded; repeatedly grand ministers were driven out.
translations.idiomatic: By then Wei Zhongxian was steadily amassing power, the outer court falling in line, and senior ministers were being driven out one after another.

sentences.zh: 震孟憤，於是冬十月上《勤政講學疏》，言：「今四方多故，無歲不蹙地陷城，覆軍殺將，乃大小臣工臥薪嘗膽之日。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng was indignant; in the tenth month of that winter he submitted "Memorial on Diligent Rule and Lecturing," saying: "Now the four directions have many troubles; no year passes without lost territory and fallen cities, armies destroyed and generals killed—this is the day for officials great and small to sleep on brushwood and taste gall.
translations.idiomatic: Indignant, Zhenmeng that winter submitted his Memorial on Diligent Rule and Lecturing, writing, "The realm is beset on every side; year after year territory is lost and cities fall, armies are wiped out and commanders killed—this is when every official, high and low, must brace himself as if sleeping on brushwood and tasting gall.

sentences.zh: 而因循粉飾，將使祖宗天下日銷月削。

translations.literal: Yet dragging feet and putting on cosmetics will cause the ancestral empire day by day to dwindle month by month.
translations.idiomatic: Yet if we go on dawdling and papering things over, the empire our ancestors built will erode day by day and month by month.

sentences.zh: 非陛下大破常格，鼓舞豪傑心，天下事未知所終也。

translations.literal: Unless Your Majesty greatly breaks routine patterns and stirs the hearts of the bold, the affairs of the empire—who knows where they will end.
translations.idiomatic: Unless Your Majesty boldly breaks with routine and fires the hearts of the able, there is no telling where the realm will end up.

sentences.zh: 陛下昧爽臨朝，寒暑靡輟，政非不勤，然鴻臚引奏，跪拜起立，如傀儡登場已耳。

translations.literal: Your Majesty attends court at dawn, never ceasing in cold or heat—the government is not undiligent; yet when the Court of State Ceremonial presents memorials, kneeling and rising, it is like puppets taking the stage—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty holds court at dawn through every season—no one can call you idle. Yet when the Court of State Ceremonial leads memorials forward and officials kneel and rise in turn, it is no more than puppets treading a stage.

sentences.zh: 請按祖宗制，唱六部六科，則六部六科以次白事，糾彈敷奏，陛下與輔弼大臣面裁決焉。

translations.literal: I beg according to the ancestral system to call the six ministries and six offices, then the six ministries and six offices in turn report affairs, impeach and present memorials, and Your Majesty with assisting grand ministers decide face to face.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that we restore the ancestral practice of calling the six ministries and six censorial offices in turn to report business, impeach, and petition, so that Your Majesty and the grand secretaries may decide matters face to face.

sentences.zh: 則聖智日益明習，而百執事各有奮心。

translations.literal: Then sagely wisdom daily grows clear and practiced, and the hundred officials each have zeal.
translations.idiomatic: Your wisdom would grow sharper by the day, and every official would find renewed purpose.

sentences.zh: 若僅揭帖一紙，長跪一諾，北面一揖，安取此鴛行豸繡、橫玉腰金者為？

translations.literal: If only posting a slip of paper, long kneeling one assent, north-facing one bow—what use these paired-mandarin-duck ranks, unicorn-badge embroidery, jade girdle pendants, and gold belts?
translations.idiomatic: If all that is required is to submit a slip, kneel long, murmur assent, and bow toward the throne, what need is there for officials bearing mandarin-duck insignia, unicorn badges, jade pendants, and gold belts?

sentences.zh: 經筵日講，臨禦有期，學非不講，然侍臣進讀，鋪敘文辭，如蒙師誦說已耳。

translations.literal: At the classics sessions daily lectures, the emperor presides on schedule—learning is not untaught; yet lecturing officials read aloud, laying out literary phrases like a village teacher reciting—that is all.
translations.idiomatic: The daily classics lectures are held on schedule and learning is not neglected—yet the lecturing officials merely recite fine phrases like village schoolmasters droning through a text.

sentences.zh: 祖宗之朝，君臣相對，如家人父子。

translations.literal: In the ancestral court, lord and minister faced each other like family, father and son.
translations.idiomatic: In the days of our forefathers emperor and minister spoke as freely as father and son within a household.

sentences.zh: 咨訪軍國重事，閭閻隱微，情形畢照，奸詐無所藏，左右近習亦無緣蒙蔽。

translations.literal: Consulting on military and state weighty affairs, hidden matters in lanes and alleys—all conditions fully illuminated; treachery has nowhere to hide; those close at hand also have no chance to deceive.
translations.idiomatic: They consulted on weighty matters of war and state and on hidden troubles among the people; nothing escaped view, fraud had nowhere to hide, and even those closest to the throne could not mislead him.

sentences.zh: 若僅尊嚴如神，上下拱手，經傳典謨徒循故事，安取此正笏垂紳、展書簪筆者為？

translations.literal: If only august as a god, above and below bow with folded hands, classics and precepts merely follow old cases—what use these upright tablets, draped sashes, opened books, and pinned brushes?
translations.idiomatic: If the throne is remote as a god, courtesies are exchanged in silence, and the classics are recited as empty ritual, what purpose is served by scholars holding their tablets, robes falling in order, books spread open, and brushes tucked in their caps?

sentences.zh: 且陛下既與群臣不洽，朝夕侍禦不越中涓之輩，豈知帝王宏遠規模？

translations.literal: Moreover Your Majesty, already not in harmony with the multitude of ministers, day and night attend and serve none beyond the middle eunuchs—how can one know the emperor's broad far-reaching designs?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty is estranged from his ministers and day and night sees only palace eunuchs, how can you grasp the emperor's wider vision?

sentences.zh: 於是危如山海，而閣臣一出，莫挽偷安之習；

translations.literal: Thus perilous as mountains and seas, yet when a grand secretary goes out, no one can reverse the habit of stealing ease;
translations.idiomatic: Peril mounts like mountains and seas, yet when a grand secretary steps in, no one can break the habit of complacency;

sentences.zh: 慘如黔圍，而撫臣坐視，不聞嚴譴之施。

translations.literal: Desperate as the siege of Qian, yet grand coordinators sit watching, and one hears no severe reprimand applied.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster spreads like the siege of Qian, yet provincial governors sit idle and no stern punishment follows.

sentences.zh: 近日舉動，尤可異者。

translations.literal: Recent actions are especially strange.
translations.idiomatic: Recent conduct has been especially alarming.

sentences.zh: 鄒元標去位，馮從吾杜門，首揆冢宰亦相率求退。

translations.literal: Zou Yuanbiao left office, Feng Congwu closed his door, the chief grand secretary and chief minister also one after another sought withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: Zou Yuanbiao has left office, Feng Congwu has shut his door, and even the chief grand secretary and chief minister have one after another asked to resign.

sentences.zh: 空人國以營私窟，幾似濁流之投；

translations.literal: Emptying the state's people to build private lairs—almost like casting into muddy streams;
translations.idiomatic: The state is emptied so private factions may build their nests—almost as if filth were being poured into the stream;

sentences.zh: 詈道學以逐名賢，有甚偽學之禁。

translations.literal: Reviling the Learning of the Way to drive out famed worthies—worse than the ban on false learning.
translations.idiomatic: Abusing the Learning of the Way to purge worthy men—a prohibition worse than the "False Learning" purge of old.

sentences.zh: 唐、宋末季，可為前鑒。

translations.literal: The late ages of Tang and Song can serve as prior mirrors.
translations.idiomatic: The late Tang and Song dynasties stand as warnings before us.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，忠賢屏不即奏。

translations.literal: " When the memorial entered, Zhongxian blocked it and did not immediately present it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, Zhongxian kept it from the Emperor and did not present it at once.

sentences.zh: 乘帝觀劇，摘疏中「傀儡登場」語，謂比帝於偶人，不殺無以示天下，帝頷之。

translations.literal: Seizing when the emperor was watching a play, he picked the phrase "puppets taking the stage" from the memorial, saying it compared the emperor to wooden figures—without killing, there is no way to show the empire; the emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: Waiting until the Emperor was watching a play, he seized on the phrase "puppets taking the stage," claiming Zhenmeng had compared the Emperor to wooden dolls and saying he must die to give the realm an example; the Emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 一日，講筵畢，忠賢傳旨，廷杖震孟八十。

translations.literal: One day, when the lecture session ended, Zhongxian transmitted the decree: court bastinado of Zhenmeng eighty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: One day, as the lecture session ended, Zhongxian relayed an order that Zhenmeng be beaten eighty strokes in court.

sentences.zh: 首輔葉向高在告，次輔韓爌力爭。

translations.literal: Chief grand secretary Ye Xianggao was on leave; secondary grand secretary Han Kuang argued forcefully.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Grand Secretary Ye Xianggao was on leave, but Secondary Grand Secretary Han Kuang protested fiercely.

sentences.zh: 會庶吉士鄭鄤疏復入，內批俱貶秩調外。

translations.literal: Just then the bachelor Zheng Man's memorial also entered; an inner rescript demoted both in rank and transferred them outside.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time a memorial from Hanlin bachelor Zheng Man reached the throne; an inner rescript demoted both men and transferred them to posts outside the capital.

sentences.zh: 言官交章論救，不納。

translations.literal: Censorial officials submitted successive memorials pleading for rescue; it was not accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Censors petitioned one after another on their behalf, but the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 震孟亦不赴調而歸。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng also did not go to his transfer and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng likewise refused his assignment and went home.

sentences.zh: 六年冬，太倉進士顧同寅、生員孫文豸坐以詩悼惜熊廷弼，為兵馬司緝獲。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, winter, the Taicang jinshi Gu Tongyin and licentiate Sun Wenchi were apprehended by the military patrol office for writing poems mourning and grieving Xiong Tingbi.
translations.idiomatic: That winter in the sixth year the Taicang jinshi Gu Tongyin and student Sun Wenchi were seized by the city patrol for poems lamenting Xiong Tingbi's fate.

sentences.zh: 御史門克新指為妖言，波及震孟，與編修陳仁錫、庶吉士鄭鄤並斥為民。

translations.literal: Censor Men Kexin pointed to it as heterodox speech; it spread to Zhenmeng, and together with compiler Chen Renxi and bachelor Zheng Man all were expelled to commoner status.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Men Kexin denounced the poems as seditious talk; the case implicated Zhenmeng, and he was stripped of rank along with Compiler Chen Renxi and Bachelor Zheng Man.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年以侍讀召。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he was summoned as lecturing reader.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen 1 he was recalled as Lecturer-in-Waiting.

sentences.zh: 改左中允，充日講官。

translations.literal: He was changed to Left Messenger and filled the post of daily lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Left Messenger and served as a daily lecturer at court.

sentences.zh: 三年春，輔臣定逆案者相繼去國，忠賢遺黨王永光輩日乘機報復，震孟抗疏糾之。

translations.literal: In the third year, spring, assisting ministers who settled the treason cases left the state one after another; Zhongxian's remnant faction Wang Yongguang and others daily seized opportunity for revenge; Zhenmeng submitted a resisting memorial to impeach them.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the ministers who had settled Wei Zhongxian's treason case were leaving office one after another; survivors of Zhongxian's faction such as Wang Yongguang were daily seizing chances for revenge, and Zhenmeng memorialized against them.

sentences.zh: 帝方眷永光，不報。

translations.literal: The emperor was then favoring Yongguang; no reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was still favoring Yongguang, and no answer came.

sentences.zh: 震孟尋進左諭德，掌司經局，直講如故。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng soon was promoted to Left Instructor, directed the Classics Bureau, and lectured as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng was soon promoted to Left Instructor, put in charge of the Classics Bureau, and continued lecturing as before.

sentences.zh: 五月，復上疏曰：「群小合謀，欲借邊才翻逆案。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he again submitted a memorial saying: "Petty men conspire, wishing to use border talent to overturn the treason cases.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he memorialized again: "Petty men are conspiring to use frontier appointments to reopen the treason cases.

sentences.zh: 天下有無才誤事之君子，必無懷忠報國之小人。

translations.literal: Under heaven there are upright gentlemen whose lack of talent causes errors, but there are certainly no petty men who harbor loyalty and repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: The realm has no shortage of decent men who lack talent and blunder—but it has no petty men who truly serve the state in loyalty.

sentences.zh: 今有平生無恥，慘殺名賢之呂純如，且藉奧援思辯雪。

translations.literal: Now there is Lu Chunru, shameless all his life, who cruelly killed a famed worthy, and moreover relying on hidden backing seeks to argue for vindication.
translations.idiomatic: Now there is Lu Chunru—shameless his whole life, who had a celebrated worthy brutally killed—and he even seeks rehabilitation through court connections.

sentences.zh: 永光為六卿長，假竊威福，倒置用舍，無事不專而濟以狠，發念必欺而飾以樸，以年例大典而變亂祖制，以考選盛舉而擯斥清才。

translations.literal: Yongguang as head of the six ministers falsely stole authority and blessing, inverted appointment and dismissal; in nothing was he not willful, aided by harshness; in every intent he deceived yet adorned with simplicity; using the annual precedent great ceremony to overturn ancestral institutions; using the examination selection grand event to reject clear talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yongguang, as senior among the six ministers, usurped authority at every turn, reversing merit and dismissal as he pleased—arrogant in all things and ruthless in support, cunning in every scheme yet cloaking himself in plain virtue, using the annual review to upend ancestral practice and the civil-service examinations to shut out men of merit.

sentences.zh: 舉朝震恐，莫敢訟言。

translations.literal: The whole court trembled in fear; none dared speak in dispute.
translations.idiomatic: The whole court stood in dread and no one dared speak out.

sentences.zh: 臣下雷同，豈國之福！

translations.literal: Subjects echoing alike—how is this the state's blessing!
translations.idiomatic: When every official parrots the same line, what blessing is that for the state?

sentences.zh: 」帝令指實再奏。

translations.literal: " The emperor ordered him to specify facts and memorial again.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered him to name names and submit another memorial with specifics.

sentences.zh: 震孟言：「殺名賢者，故吏部郎周順昌。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng said: "The killer of the famed worthy was the former Ministry of Personnel Director Zhou Shunchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng replied, "The man who had the worthy killed was the late Director Zhou Shunchang of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 年例則抑吏科都給事中陳良訓，考選則擯中書舍人陳士奇、潘有功是也。

translations.literal: For the annual precedent it was suppressing Chief Supervising Secretary Chen Liangxun of the Personnel Office; for examination selection it was rejecting Secretariat Drafters Chen Shiji and Pan Yougong.
translations.idiomatic: The annual review case was the suppression of Chief Supervising Secretary Chen Liangxun of the Personnel Office; the examination case was the rejection of Secretariat Drafters Chen Shiji and Pan Yougong.

sentences.zh: 」永光窘甚，密結大奄王永祚謂士奇出姚希孟門，震孟，希孟舅也。

translations.literal: " Yongguang was greatly embarrassed; secretly he allied with grand eunuch Wang Yongzuo, saying Shiji came from Yao Ximeng's school—Zhenmeng was Ximeng's maternal uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Mortified, Yongguang secretly colluded with the senior eunuch Wang Yongzuo, claiming Shiji had been a protégé of Yao Ximeng—and Zhenmeng was Ximeng's uncle.

sentences.zh: 帝心疑之。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart suspected it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor grew suspicious.

sentences.zh: 永光辯疏得溫旨，而責震孟任情牽詆。

translations.literal: Yongguang's defending memorial received a warm edict, while Zhenmeng was blamed for arbitrary dragging accusations.
translations.idiomatic: Yongguang's defense received a soothing imperial reply, while Zhenmeng was rebuked for reckless accusations.

sentences.zh: 然群小翻案之謀亦由是中沮。

translations.literal: Yet the petty men's scheme to overturn cases thereby was also blocked midway.
translations.idiomatic: Still, the petty faction's plan to reopen the treason cases was stopped in its tracks.

sentences.zh: 震孟在講筵，最嚴正。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng at the lecture sessions was most strict and upright.
translations.idiomatic: At the lecture sessions Zhenmeng was stern and upright above all others.

sentences.zh: 時大臣數逮系，震孟講《魯論》「君使臣以禮」一章，反覆規諷，帝即降旨出尚書喬允升、侍郎胡世賞於獄。

translations.literal: At the time many grand ministers were repeatedly arrested and imprisoned; Zhenmeng lectured on the Analects chapter "The lord employs his ministers with propriety," repeatedly admonishing by indirect criticism; the emperor immediately issued an edict releasing Ministers Qiao Yunsheng and Vice Minister Hu Shishang from prison.
translations.idiomatic: When several senior ministers were being arrested one after another, Zhenmeng lectured on the Analects passage "If the ruler treats his ministers with propriety," admonishing the Emperor again and again by indirection; the Emperor promptly ordered Ministers Qiao Yunsheng and Vice Minister Hu Shishang released from prison.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗足加於膝，適講《五子之歌》，至「為人上者，奈何不敬」，以目視帝足，帝即袖掩之，徐為引下。

translations.literal: The emperor once placed his foot on his knee; just as he was lecturing on the "Songs of the Five Sons," reaching "for one who stands above others, how can one not be reverent," he looked with his eyes at the emperor's foot; the emperor immediately covered it with his sleeve and slowly drew it down.
translations.idiomatic: Once, as the Emperor rested his foot on his knee, Zhenmeng was lecturing on the Songs of the Five Sons and came to the line, "Those who stand above others—how can they fail to be reverent?" He glanced at the Emperor's foot; the Emperor at once hid it in his sleeve and slowly withdrew it.

sentences.zh: 時稱「真講官」。

translations.literal: At the time he was called "a true lecturer."
translations.idiomatic: People of the day called him a lecturer in the true sense of the word.

sentences.zh: 既忤權臣，欲避去。

translations.literal: Having already offended a powerful minister, he wished to withdraw and leave.
translations.idiomatic: After offending a powerful minister, he sought to withdraw from office.

sentences.zh: 出封益府，便道歸，遂不復出。

translations.literal: He went out on assignment to the Yi princely establishment, returned home by the direct route, and never came out again.
translations.idiomatic: Sent on duty to the Yi princely establishment, he took the opportunity to return home and never entered service again.

sentences.zh: 五年，即家擢右庶子。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, while at home he was promoted to Right Sub-Expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chongzhen, he was promoted to Right Sub-Expositor while still at home.

sentences.zh: 久之，進少詹事。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was advanced to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 初，天啟時，詔修《光宗實錄》，禮部侍郎周炳謨載神宗時儲位臲卼及「妖書」、「梃擊」諸事，直筆無所阿。

translations.literal: Initially, during the Tianqi reign, an edict ordered the compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Guangzong. Vice Minister of Rites Zhou Bingmo recorded the perilous situation of the crown prince during Emperor Shenzong's time and such matters as the "Demonic Book" and "Club Assault" incidents, writing with a straight brush and flattering no one.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Tianqi reign, the court ordered the compilation of the Veritable Records of Emperor Guangzong. Vice Minister of Rites Zhou Bingmo recorded the peril surrounding the heir apparent under Emperor Shenzong, along with the Demonic Book and Club Assault affairs, writing truthfully without deferring to anyone.
