sentences.zh: 其後忠賢盜柄，御史石三畏劾削炳謨職。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhongxian usurped power; Censor Shi Sanwei memorialized to strip Bingmo of his office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Wei Zhongxian seized power, Censor Shi Sanwei impeached Zhou Bingmo and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 忠賢使其黨重修，是非倒置。

translations.literal: Zhongxian had his faction recompile it, right and wrong inverted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxian had his clique revise the records, reversing right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 震孟摘尤謬者數條，疏請改正。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng selected several of the most egregious errors and submitted a memorial requesting correction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng singled out several of the worst errors and submitted a memorial asking that they be corrected.

sentences.zh: 帝特禦平臺，召廷臣面議，卒為溫體仁、王應熊所沮。

translations.literal: The emperor specially attended the Level Platform in person, summoned court ministers to debate face to face, but in the end was blocked by Wen Tiren and Wang Yingxiong.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor personally presided at the Level Platform and summoned the court to debate the matter face to face, but in the end Wen Tiren and Wang Yingxiong blocked the proposal.

sentences.zh: 八年正月，賊犯鳳陽皇陵。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighth year, bandits attacked the imperial mausoleum at Fengyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighth year, rebels attacked the imperial tombs at Fengyang.

sentences.zh: 震孟歷陳致亂之源，因言：「當事諸臣，不能憂國奉公，一統之朝，強分畛域，加膝墜淵，總由恩怨。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng set forth in detail the sources of disorder, then said: "The ministers in charge cannot worry for the state and serve with public devotion; in a unified court they forcibly divide spheres, treating some as close as bringing knee to knee and others as distant as dropping into an abyss—all because of personal grudges and favors.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng traced in detail the roots of the chaos and said: "Those who hold office cannot put the state's interests first or serve selflessly. In a court that ought to be one, they carve out rival camps, raising favorites to their knees and casting enemies into the abyss—all of it driven by private resentment and patronage.

sentences.zh: 數年來，振綱肅紀者何事，推賢用能者何人，安內攘外者何道，富國強兵者何策？

translations.literal: Over these many years, what has been done to tighten discipline and restore order? Who has been promoted for talent and ability? What course has been taken to pacify within and repel without? What policy has been adopted to enrich the state and strengthen the army?
translations.idiomatic: For years now, what have they done to restore discipline? Whom have they raised up for merit and ability? What means have they used to secure the interior and drive off foreign threats? What strategy have they pursued to make the state rich and the army strong?

sentences.zh: 陛下宜奮然一怒，發哀痛之詔，按失律之誅，正誤國之罪，行撫綏之實政，寬閭閻之積逋。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should rouse yourself in anger, issue a proclamation of mourning and repentance, punish those who violated discipline, rectify the crimes of those who misled the state, carry out policies that truly pacify the people, and remit the accumulated arrears owed by common households.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should summon a righteous wrath, proclaim your grief and remorse, punish those who failed in duty, hold accountable those who have misled the state, enact policies that genuinely bring order to the people, and forgive the long-standing tax debts of the common folk.

sentences.zh: 先收人心以遏寇盜，徐議浚財之源，毋徒竭澤而漁。

translations.literal: First gather the people's hearts to check bandits and robbers; then discuss gradually reopening sources of revenue—do not merely drain the pond to catch the fish.
translations.idiomatic: First win back the people's loyalty to check rebellion; only then discuss how to reopen the springs of revenue—not simply drain the marshes dry for a single catch.

sentences.zh: 盡斥患得患失之鄙夫，廣集群策群力以定亂，國事庶有瘳乎！

translations.literal: Drive out entirely the petty men who cling to office fearing loss; broadly gather collective plans and combined strength to settle the disorder—then perhaps state affairs can be healed!
translations.idiomatic: Expel every petty official who clings to rank out of fear of loss; rally every counsel and every strength to quell the chaos—then perhaps the state may yet recover!

sentences.zh: 」帝優旨報之，然亦不能盡行也。

translations.literal: " The emperor replied with gracious edicts, yet could not fully carry it out either.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor responded with a gracious edict, yet he could not put the recommendations fully into practice.

sentences.zh: 故事，講筵不列《春秋》。

translations.literal: By precedent, the Spring and Autumn Annals were not included in the lecture curriculum.
translations.idiomatic: By established practice, the Spring and Autumn Annals were not part of the imperial lecture program.

sentences.zh: 帝以有裨治亂，令擇人進講。

translations.literal: The emperor, deeming it beneficial for governing disorder, ordered that lecturers be selected to lecture on it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, believing it useful for understanding order and chaos, ordered suitable lecturers chosen to expound it.

sentences.zh: 震孟，《春秋》名家，為體仁所忌，隱不舉。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng was a master of the Spring and Autumn; Tiren envied him and secretly did not recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng was a celebrated scholar of the Spring and Autumn Annals, but Tiren envied him and quietly omitted his name.

sentences.zh: 次輔錢士升指及之，體仁佯驚曰：「幾失此人！

translations.literal: Second Assistant Qian Shisheng pointed to him; Tiren feigned surprise and said: "We nearly lost this man!
translations.idiomatic: Second Assistant Qian Shisheng mentioned him, whereupon Tiren feigned astonishment and said, "We nearly overlooked this man!

sentences.zh: 」遂以其名上。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted his name upward.
translations.idiomatic: He then forwarded Zhenmeng's name to the throne.

sentences.zh: 及進講，果稱帝旨。

translations.literal: When he entered to lecture, it indeed matched the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenmeng delivered his lectures, they proved exactly what the Emperor had hoped to hear.

sentences.zh: 六月，帝將增置閣臣，召廷臣數十人，試以票擬。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, the emperor was about to add Grand Secretaries; he summoned several dozen court ministers and tested them with draft response assignments.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month the Emperor planned to add Grand Secretaries and summoned several dozen ministers to a test in drafting memorial responses.

sentences.zh: 震孟引疾不入，體仁方在告。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng cited illness and did not attend; Tiren happened to be on leave.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng pleaded illness and stayed away; Tiren happened to be on sick leave.

sentences.zh: 七月，帝特擢震孟禮部左侍郎兼東閣大學士，入閣預政。

translations.literal: In the seventh month, the emperor specially promoted Zhenmeng to Left Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the cabinet to participate in government.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month the Emperor specially promoted Zhenmeng to Left Vice Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, bringing him into the cabinet.

sentences.zh: 兩疏固辭，不許。

translations.literal: Twice he submitted memorials firmly declining; [the emperor] did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He twice memorialized a firm refusal, but the Emperor would not accept it.

sentences.zh: 閣臣被命，即投刺司禮大奄，兼致儀狀，震孟獨否。

translations.literal: Grand secretaries upon receiving appointment would immediately send visiting cards to the chief eunuch of the Directorate of Ceremonial, also presenting ceremonial gifts; Zhenmeng alone did not.
translations.idiomatic: Upon appointment, Grand Secretaries customarily paid courtesy calls on the Director of Ceremonial eunuchs and sent formal gifts; Zhenmeng alone refused.

sentences.zh: 掌司禮者曹化淳，故屬王安從奄，雅慕震孟，令人輾轉道意，卒不往。

translations.literal: The one in charge of the Directorate of Ceremonial was Cao Huachun, formerly a follower-eunuch of Wang An, who had always admired Zhenmeng; he sent someone to convey his intentions through intermediaries, but in the end Zhenmeng did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the Directorate of Ceremonial was Cao Huachun, once a follower of the eunuch Wang An, who had long admired Zhenmeng. Through intermediaries Cao repeatedly expressed his wish to meet; Zhenmeng never went.

sentences.zh: 震孟既入直，體仁每擬旨必商之，有所改必從，喜謂人曰：「溫公虛懷，何雲奸也？

translations.literal: After Zhenmeng entered daily attendance, whenever Tiren drafted edicts he would always consult him; whenever there were changes Zhenmeng always agreed; delighted, he told others: "Master Wen is broad-minded—how can one call him treacherous?
translations.idiomatic: Once in office, Zhenmeng found that whenever Tiren drafted an edict he consulted him first and always accepted his revisions. Delighted, Zhenmeng told others, "Master Wen is open-minded—how can anyone call him a schemer?

sentences.zh: 」同官何吾騶曰：「此人機深，詎可輕信？

translations.literal: " Colleague He Wuzao said: "This man is deeply cunning—how can he be lightly trusted?
translations.idiomatic: His colleague He Wuzao said, "That man is deeply cunning—how can you trust him so readily?

sentences.zh: 」越十余日，體仁窺其疏，所擬不當，輒令改，不從，則徑抹去。

translations.literal: " After a dozen or so days, Tiren examined his memorial drafts; when the proposed text was unsuitable he would order changes; if Zhenmeng did not comply, he would simply strike it out.
translations.idiomatic: A little over ten days later Tiren began scrutinizing his drafts. Whenever he found wording he disliked, he ordered changes; if Zhenmeng refused, Tiren simply struck the passage out.

sentences.zh: 震孟大慍，以諸疏擲體仁前，體仁亦不顧。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng was greatly angry; he threw the memorials before Tiren; Tiren paid no attention.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Zhenmeng flung the memorials down before Tiren, who ignored him.

sentences.zh: 都給事中許譽卿者，故劾忠賢有聲，震孟及吾騶欲用為南京太常卿。

translations.literal: Chief supervising secretary Xu Yuqing had formerly impeached Zhongxian with renown; Zhenmeng and Wuzao wished to appoint him Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices at Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Supervising Secretary Xu Yuqing had gained renown for impeaching Wei Zhongxian. Zhenmeng and He Wuzao wanted to appoint him Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 體仁忌譽卿伉直，諷吏部尚書謝升劾其與福建布政使申紹芳營求美官。

translations.literal: Tiren envied Yuqing's upright and straightforward nature; he insinuated to Minister of Personnel Xie Sheng to impeach him for colluding with Fujian Administrative Commissioner Shen Shaofang to seek a fine office.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren resented Yuqing's blunt integrity and prompted Minister of Personnel Xie Sheng to impeach him for conspiring with Fujian Administrative Commissioner Shen Shaofang to procure a lucrative post.

sentences.zh: 體仁擬以貶謫，度帝欲重擬必發改，已而果然。

translations.literal: Tiren drafted a demotion and dismissal, estimating that if the emperor wished to impose a heavier penalty he would certainly send it back for revision—and so it proved.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren drafted a reduced punishment, calculating that if the Emperor wanted something harsher he would send the draft back for revision—and that is exactly what happened.

sentences.zh: 遂擬斥譽卿為民，紹芳提問。

translations.literal: Thereupon he drafted expelling Yuqing to commoner status and ordering Shaofang brought up for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: He then drafted the dismissal of Yuqing to commoner status and the summoning of Shaofang for investigation.

sentences.zh: 震孟爭之不得，咈然曰：「科道為民，是天下極榮事，賴公玉成之。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng argued but could not prevail; indignant, he said: "For a censor to be reduced to commoner status is the supreme honor under heaven—thanks to you, sir, for bringing it about.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng protested in vain, then said bitterly, "For a censor to be stripped to commoner rank is the highest honor in the realm—thanks to you for making it happen.

sentences.zh: 」體仁遽以聞。

translations.literal: " Tiren immediately reported this to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Tiren at once reported the remark to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝果怒，責吾騶、震孟徇私撓亂。

translations.literal: The emperor was indeed enraged and rebuked Wuzao and Zhenmeng for showing favoritism and obstructing the proceedings.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was indeed furious and rebuked He Wuzao and Zhenmeng for favoritism and obstruction.

sentences.zh: 吾騶罷，震孟落職閑住。

translations.literal: Wuzao was dismissed; Zhenmeng was removed from office and left idle.
translations.idiomatic: He Wuzao was dismissed; Zhenmeng was stripped of his post and sent home.

sentences.zh: 方震孟之拜命也，即有旨撤鎮守中官。

translations.literal: Just when Zhenmeng received his appointment, there was already an edict withdrawing the palace eunuchs stationed as military overseers.
translations.idiomatic: No sooner had Zhenmeng taken office than an edict went out recalling the palace eunuchs serving as military overseers.

sentences.zh: 及次輔王應熊之去，忌者謂震孟為之。

translations.literal: When Second Assistant Wang Yingxiong departed, those who envied Zhenmeng said he had engineered it.
translations.idiomatic: When Second Assistant Wang Yingxiong left office, Zhenmeng's enemies claimed he had orchestrated it.

sentences.zh: 由是有譖其居功者，帝意遂移。

translations.literal: Hence there were those who slandered him for claiming credit; the emperor's attitude shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Slander then spread that Zhenmeng had taken credit for the change, and the Emperor's regard turned against him.

sentences.zh: 震孟剛方貞介，有古大臣風，惜三月而斥，未竟其用。

translations.literal: Zhenmeng was upright, principled, and incorruptible, with the bearing of the great ministers of antiquity; alas, dismissed after three months, his talent was not fully used.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenmeng was upright, principled, and incorruptible, with the air of the great ministers of old; yet after only three months he was dismissed and his abilities were never fully employed.

sentences.zh: 歸半歲，會甥姚希孟卒，哭之慟，亦卒。

translations.literal: Half a year after returning home, his nephew Yao Ximu died; he wept for him in deep grief and also died.
translations.idiomatic: Six months after returning home, his nephew Yao Ximu died. Zhenmeng mourned him so bitterly that he too fell ill and died.

sentences.zh: 廷臣請恤，不允。

translations.literal: Court ministers requested posthumous grants; [the emperor] did not grant them.
translations.idiomatic: The court requested posthumous honors for him, but the Emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 十二年，詔復故官。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, an edict restored his former office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, an edict restored his former rank.

sentences.zh: 十五年，贈禮部尚書，賜祭葬，官一子。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Rites, granted sacrificial rites and burial honors, and one son was given an official appointment.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was posthumously made Minister of Rites, granted state funeral rites, and one son received an official appointment.

sentences.zh: 福王時，追謚文肅。

translations.literal: During the reign of the Prince of Fu, he was posthumously given the posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Fu he was posthumously granted the temple name Wensu.

sentences.zh: 二子秉、乘。

translations.literal: Two sons: Bing and Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons, Bing and Cheng.

sentences.zh: 乘遭國變，死於難。

translations.literal: Cheng met the dynastic catastrophe and died in the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng perished in the cataclysm that befell the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 周炳謨，子仲覲，無錫人。

translations.literal: Zhou Bingmo, style name Zhongjing, was a man of Wuxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Bingmo, styled Zhongjing, was a native of Wuxi.

sentences.zh: 父子義，嘉靖中庶吉士，萬歷中仕至吏部侍郎，卒謚文恪。

translations.literal: His father Ziyi, a presented scholar in the Jiajing reign, served through the Wanli reign to Vice Minister of Personnel; upon death he was given the posthumous title Wenge.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhou Ziyi, a presented scholar under Jiajing, rose under Wanli to Vice Minister of Personnel and was posthumously titled Wenge.

sentences.zh: 炳謨，萬歷三十二年進士。

translations.literal: Bingmo, a jinshi of the thirty-second year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Bingmo passed the jinshi examination in the thirty-second year of Wanli.

sentences.zh: 當重修《光宗實錄》時，炳謨已先卒。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Emperor Guangzong were to be recompiled, Bingmo had already died earlier.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the Veritable Records of Emperor Guangzong were being revised, Bingmo had already died.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，贈禮部尚書，謚文簡。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chongzhen, he was posthumously enfeoffed Minister of Rites and given the posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of Chongzhen he was posthumously made Minister of Rites with the posthumous title Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 父子皆以學行稱於世。

translations.literal: Father and son were both renowned in the world for learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Both father and son were celebrated throughout the realm for scholarship and character.

sentences.zh: 蔣德璟，字申葆，晉江人。

translations.literal: Jiang Dejing, style name Shenbao, was a man of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Dejing, styled Shenbao, was a native of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 父光彥，江西副使。

translations.literal: His father Guangyan was a vice commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jiang Guangyan served as Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 德璟，天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: Dejing, a jinshi of the second year of Tianqi.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing passed the jinshi examination in the second year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He was transferred to presented scholar, appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Hanlin as a presented scholar and was appointed Compiler.

sentences.zh: 崇禎時，由侍讀歷遷少詹事，條奏救荒事宜。

translations.literal: During Chongzhen, from Reader-in-Waiting he was promoted in succession to Junior Tutor and submitted memorials outlining famine relief measures.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he rose from Reader-in-Waiting to Junior Tutor and submitted detailed proposals for famine relief.

sentences.zh: 尋擢禮部右侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Right Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 時議限民田，德璟言：「民田不可奪，而足食莫如貴粟。

translations.literal: At the time there was discussion of limiting private landholding; Dejing said: "Private land cannot be seized, and nothing secures food better than keeping grain valuable.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated capping private landholdings, Dejing argued: "Private land must not be confiscated; the surest way to ensure food is to keep grain prices high.

sentences.zh: 北平、山、陜、江北諸處，宜聽民開墾，及課種桑棗，修農田水利。

translations.literal: In Beiping, Shanxi, Shaanxi, and northern Jiangsu and other places, the people should be allowed to open wasteland, and taxes should be levied for planting mulberry and jujube, and for repairing farmland irrigation.
translations.idiomatic: In Beiping, Shanxi, Shaanxi, and northern Jiangsu, people should be encouraged to reclaim wasteland, plant mulberry and jujube, and repair irrigation works.

sentences.zh: 府縣官考滿，以是為殿最。

translations.literal: When prefectural and county officials completed their tenure examinations, this should be the standard for ranking best and worst.
translations.idiomatic: When prefects and magistrates came up for performance review, these measures should weigh most heavily in their ratings.

sentences.zh: 至常平義倉，歲輸本色，依令甲行之足矣。

translations.literal: As for the Ever-Normal and Charity Granaries, delivering grain in kind each year according to the regulations would be sufficient.
translations.idiomatic: As for the Ever-Normal and Charity Granaries, delivering grain in kind each year as regulations require would suffice.

sentences.zh: 」十四年春，楊嗣昌卒於軍，命九卿議罪。

translations.literal: " In the spring of the fourteenth year Yang Sichang died in camp; the emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to deliberate on penalties.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourteenth year Yang Sichang died in the field; the Emperor ordered the Nine Ministers to determine what penalties applied.

sentences.zh: 德璟議曰：「嗣昌倡聚斂之議，加剿餉、練餉，致天下民窮財盡，胥為盜，又匿失事，飾首功。

translations.literal: Dejing's deliberation said: "Sichang advocated schemes of forced levies, adding the 'bandit-suppression' and 'training' surcharges, causing the people under heaven to be destitute and funds exhausted, all becoming bandits; moreover he concealed defeats and embellished the first reported victories.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing's finding read: "Sichang championed ruthless taxation, imposing the bandit-suppression and training surtaxes until the people were ruined and the treasury empty and men turned to banditry; he also hid defeats and invented victory reports.

sentences.zh: 宜按仇鸞事，追正其罪。

translations.literal: He should be handled according to the case of Qiu Luan, and his crimes corrected after the fact.
translations.idiomatic: His case should be handled like Qiu Luan's, with his crimes formally corrected posthumously.

sentences.zh: 」不從。

translations.literal: " [The emperor] did not follow this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor did not accept the recommendation.

sentences.zh: 十五年二月，耕耤禮成，請召還原任侍郎陳子壯、祭酒倪元璐等，帝皆錄用。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifteenth year, after the spring plowing rites were completed, he requested the recall of the former Vice Minister Chen Zizhuang, Sacrificial Official Ni Yuanlu, and others; the emperor approved and employed them all.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fifteenth year, after the spring plowing ceremony, he requested the recall of former Vice Minister Chen Zizhuang, Sacrificial Official Ni Yuanlu, and others; the Emperor approved and reinstated them all.

sentences.zh: 六月，廷推閣臣，首德璟。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, when the court nominated Grand Secretaries, Dejing headed the list.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, when Grand Secretaries were nominated, Dejing topped the list.

sentences.zh: 入對，言邊臣須久任，薊督半載更五人，事將益廢弛。

translations.literal: Entering audience, he said frontier commanders must serve long terms—half a year in Ji Province had seen five changes of governor, and affairs would only grow more lax.
translations.idiomatic: At his audience he argued that border commanders needed long tenures: in half a year Ji Province had seen five governors, and affairs would only grow more neglected.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「不稱當更。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "If they are unfit they should be changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "If they are incompetent, replace them.

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「與其更於後，曷若慎於初。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Better to choose carefully at the start than to keep changing afterward.
translations.idiomatic: He replied, "Better to choose carefully from the first than to keep replacing them later.

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「天變何由弭？

translations.literal: " The emperor asked: "How can celestial anomalies be stilled?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor asked, "How can these heavenly portents be abated?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「莫如拯百姓。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Nothing better than saving the common people.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "There is no better way than to rescue the common people.

sentences.zh: 近加遼餉千萬，練餉七百萬，民何以堪！

translations.literal: Recently the Liaodong levy was increased by ten million, the training levy by seven million—how can the people bear it!
translations.idiomatic: The Liaodong levy has lately been raised by ten million, the training levy by seven million—how can the people endure it!

sentences.zh: 祖制，三協止一督、一撫、一總兵，今增二督、三撫、六總兵，又設副將數十人，權不統一，何由制勝！

translations.literal: By ancestral regulation, the three defense zones had only one governor, one military commissioner, and one commander-in-chief; now two more governors, three more military commissioners, and six commanders-in-chief have been added, with deputy generals numbering in the dozens—authority is not unified; how can victory be achieved!
translations.idiomatic: Under ancestral practice the three defense zones had one governor, one commissioner, and one commander-in-chief; now two governors, three commissioners, and six commanders-in-chief have been added, with dozens of deputy generals—command is fragmented; how can we prevail!

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之。

translations.literal: " The emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor nodded in agreement.

sentences.zh: 首輔周延儒嘗薦德璟淵博，可備顧問，文體華贍，宜用之代言。

translations.literal: Chief Assistant Zhou Yanru once recommended Dejing as deeply learned and fit for consultation, with elegant literary style suited for drafting on the emperor's behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Assistant Zhou Yanru had recommended Dejing as deeply learned and fit for counsel, with a polished style suited to drafting imperial pronouncements.

sentences.zh: 遂擢德璟及黃景昉、吳甡為禮部尚書兼東閣大學士，同入直。

translations.literal: Thereupon Dejing, along with Huang Jingfang and Wu Shen, were promoted to Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, all entering daily attendance together.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing was accordingly promoted with Huang Jingfang and Wu Shen to Minister of Rites and concurrently Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, and all three entered the inner cabinet.

sentences.zh: 延儒、甡各樹門戶，德璟無所比。

translations.literal: Yanru and Shen each built their own factions; Dejing allied with neither.
translations.idiomatic: Yanru and Wu Shen each cultivated their own followings; Dejing attached himself to neither.

sentences.zh: 性鯁直，黃道周召用，劉宗周免罪，德璟之力居多。

translations.literal: By nature he was blunt and upright; Huang Daozhou's recall and Liu Zongzhou's lenient treatment owed much to Dejing's efforts.
translations.idiomatic: Blunt and upright by nature, he did more than anyone to bring Huang Daozhou back to office and secure leniency for Liu Zongzhou.

sentences.zh: 開封久被圍，自請馳督諸將戰，優詔不允。

translations.literal: Kaifeng had long been besieged; he volunteered to ride out and direct the generals in battle, but a gracious edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: When Kaifeng was under long siege he asked leave to ride out and direct the generals in person, but the Emperor declined in a gracious edict.

sentences.zh: 明年，進《禦覽備邊冊》，凡九邊十六鎮新舊兵食之數，及屯、鹽、民運、漕糧、馬價悉誌焉。

translations.literal: The next year he submitted the "Imperial Review Frontier Defense Register," fully recording for the nine border zones and sixteen garrisons the old and new tallies of troops and provisions, along with garrison farming, salt franchises, civilian transport, canal grain, and horse prices.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he submitted the Imperial Review Frontier Defense Register, documenting for all nine borders and sixteen garrisons the old and new figures for troops and supplies, together with garrison farming, salt monopolies, civilian transport, canal grain, and remount costs.

sentences.zh: 已，進《諸邊撫賞冊》及《禦覽簡明冊》。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he submitted the "Frontier Pacification Reward Register" and the "Imperial Review Abridged Register."
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed with the Frontier Pacification Reward Register and the Imperial Review Abridged Register.

sentences.zh: 帝深嘉之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply praised this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor commended the work in the highest terms.

sentences.zh: 諸邊士馬報戶部者，浮兵部過半，耗糧居多，而屯田、鹽引、民運，每鎮至數十百萬，一聽之邊臣。

translations.literal: Reports of frontier troops and horses submitted to the Ministry of Revenue inflated those reported to the Ministry of War by more than half; wasted provisions were the greater part, while garrison farming, salt certificates, and civilian transport—each garrison amounted to several millions—were all left entirely to frontier officials.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troop returns sent to the Ministry of Revenue inflated those sent to the Ministry of War by more than half, with wasted provisions the main excess; garrison farming, salt certificates, and civilian transport worth millions per garrison were left entirely to the border commanders.

sentences.zh: 天津海道輸薊、遼歲米豆三百萬，惟倉場督臣及天津撫臣出入，部中皆不稽核。

translations.literal: The Tianjin sea route delivered three million piculs of grain and beans annually to Ji and Liaodong; only the granary superintendent and the Tianjin governor handled receipts and disbursements—the ministries did not audit them at all.
translations.idiomatic: The Tianjin sea route shipped three million piculs of grain and beans each year to Ji and Liaodong; only the granary superintendent and the Tianjin governor managed the accounts, with no ministry oversight at all.

sentences.zh: 德璟語部臣，合部運津運、各邊民運、屯、鹽，通為計畫，餉額可足，而加派之餉可裁。

translations.literal: Dejing told the ministry officials to combine ministry transport, Tianjin transport, civilian transport on each frontier, garrison farming, and salt into one integrated plan—provision quotas could be met and supplemental levies could be cut.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing urged the ministry officials to integrate ministry transport, Tianjin transport, frontier civilian transport, garrison farming, and salt revenues into a single plan so that regular quotas could be met and emergency surtaxes reduced.

sentences.zh: 因復條十事以責部臣，然卒不能盡厘也。

translations.literal: Thereupon he again laid out ten items holding the ministry officials accountable, yet in the end they could not fully rectify matters.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted ten additional items holding the ministries accountable, yet in the end the abuses could not be fully cleared up.

sentences.zh: 一日召對，帝語及練兵。

translations.literal: One day at imperial audience the emperor spoke of training troops.
translations.idiomatic: One day at audience the Emperor raised the subject of training troops.

sentences.zh: 德璟曰：「《會典》，高皇帝教練軍士，一以弓弩刀槍行賞罰，此練軍法。

translations.literal: Dejing said: "The Collected Statutes record that the Founding Emperor trained soldiers with rewards and punishments based solely on bow, crossbow, blade, and spear—this is the law for training soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing said: "The Collected Statutes show that the Founding Emperor trained troops with rewards and punishments tied solely to bow, crossbow, blade, and spear—that is the law for training soldiers.

sentences.zh: 衛所總、小旗補役，以槍勝負為升降。

translations.literal: Guard and battalion chief and junior banner officers replenishing service used victory or defeat with the spear as the criterion for promotion or demotion.
translations.idiomatic: When guard and battalion officers of chief and junior rank filled vacancies, promotion and demotion depended on spear contests.

sentences.zh: 凡武弁比試，必騎射精嫻，方準襲替，此練將法。

translations.literal: For all military officers in comparative examination, mounted archery and skill had to be proficient before hereditary succession was permitted—this is the law for training generals.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever military officers were examined, they had to prove mastery of mounted archery before inheriting their posts—that is the law for training commanders.

sentences.zh: 豈至今方設兵？

translations.literal: Must troops be raised only now?
translations.idiomatic: Did the dynasty wait until now to raise an army?

sentences.zh: 」帝為悚然。

translations.literal: " The emperor was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was struck to silence.

sentences.zh: 又言：「祖制，各邊養軍止屯、鹽、民運三者，原無京運銀。

translations.literal: He also said: "By ancestral institution, maintaining troops on each frontier relied only on three methods—garrison farming, salt, and civilian transport; originally there was no silver transported from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "By ancestral law the frontiers fed their armies through garrison farming, salt revenues, and civilian transport alone—there was never any silver shipped from the capital.

sentences.zh: 自正統時始有數萬，迄萬歷末，亦止三百余萬。

translations.literal: Since the Zhengtong reign it began at tens of thousands; by the end of the Wanli reign it still amounted to only a little over three million.
translations.idiomatic: Capital silver shipments began in the Zhengtong era at only tens of thousands of taels; by the end of Wanli they still totaled barely three million.

sentences.zh: 今則遼餉、練餉並舊餉計二千余萬，而兵反少於往時，耗蠹乃如此。

translations.literal: Today Liaodong provisions, training levies, and the old provisions together total more than twenty million, yet troops are actually fewer than in former times—waste and corruption have reached such a point.
translations.idiomatic: Today Liaodong pay, training levies, and the old quotas together exceed twenty million taels, yet the army is smaller than ever—the waste and corruption have reached this pitch.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「文皇帝設京衛七十二，計軍四十萬。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The Martial Emperor established seventy-two capital guards, reckoning four hundred thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: " He went on: "The Martial Emperor raised seventy-two capital guards, with four hundred thousand troops on the rolls.

sentences.zh: 畿內八府，軍二十八萬。

translations.literal: In the eight prefectures within the capital region, there were two hundred eighty thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eight prefectures of the capital region alone there were two hundred eighty thousand.

sentences.zh: 又有中部、大寧、山東、河南班軍十六萬。

translations.literal: There were also one hundred sixty thousand rotating troops from the Middle Region, Dening, Shandong, and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: There were another one hundred sixty thousand rotating troops from the Middle Region, Dening, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 春秋入京操演，深得居重馭輕勢。

translations.literal: In spring and autumn they entered the capital for drilling exercises, fully achieving the strategic advantage of holding the heavy center to control the lighter periphery.
translations.idiomatic: Each spring and autumn they marched into the capital for drill, giving the dynasty the full advantage of a heavy center commanding a lighter periphery.

sentences.zh: 今皆虛冒。

translations.literal: Today all are phantom rolls and false claims.
translations.idiomatic: Today those rolls are almost entirely padded with phantom names.

sentences.zh: 且自來征討皆用衛所官軍，嘉靖末，始募兵，遂置軍不用。

translations.literal: Moreover, campaigns had always employed guard and battalion regular troops; only at the end of the Jiajing reign did recruitment of mercenaries begin, and thereafter the regular armies were set aside and unused.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, every campaign had relied on guard and battalion regulars; only at the end of Jiajing did the state begin hiring mercenaries, and thereafter the standing armies were left idle.

sentences.zh: 至加派日增，軍民兩困。

translations.literal: Eventually supplemental levies increased daily, and both soldiers and civilians were hard pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Supplemental levies kept mounting until both soldiers and civilians were crushed alike.

sentences.zh: 願憲章二祖，修復舊制。

translations.literal: I pray that Your Majesty may honor the statutes of the two Founding Emperors and restore the old institutions.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to uphold the statutes of the two Founding Emperors and restore the old system.

sentences.zh: 」帝是之，而不果行。

translations.literal: " The Emperor agreed in principle, but in the end did not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor assented in principle, but never put the plan into effect.

sentences.zh: 十七年，戶部主事蔣臣請行鈔法，言歲造三千萬貫，一貫價一兩，歲可得銀三千萬兩。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Jiang Chen, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, petitioned to implement paper currency, stating that if thirty million strings were minted each year at one tael per string, thirty million taels of silver could be raised annually.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year Jiang Chen, a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue, urged adoption of paper currency, arguing that minting thirty million strings a year at one tael per string would yield thirty million taels of silver annually.

sentences.zh: 侍郎王鰲永贊行之。

translations.literal: Vice Minister Wang Ao Yong endorsed and promoted the plan.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister Wang Ao Yong spoke in its favor.

sentences.zh: 帝特設內寶鈔局，晝夜督造，募商發賣，無一人應者。

translations.literal: The Emperor specially established the Inner Treasury Paper Currency Bureau, supervising production day and night, and solicited merchants to sell the notes—but not a single person responded.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor set up a special Inner Treasury Paper Currency Bureau, pressing production day and night and calling on merchants to sell the notes—not one answered.

sentences.zh: 德璟言：「百姓雖愚，誰肯以一金買一紙。

translations.literal: Dejing said: "Though the common people may be simple, who would pay one ounce of gold for a slip of paper?
translations.idiomatic: Dejing said, "However simple the people may be, who would trade an ounce of silver for a scrap of paper?

sentences.zh: 」帝不聽。

translations.literal: " The Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 又因局官言，責取桑穰二百萬斤於畿輔、山東、河南、浙江。

translations.literal: Then, acting on officials of the bureau, he ordered two million jin of mulberry bark pulp to be collected from the capital region, Shandong, Henan, and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Then, on the bureau officials' advice, he ordered two million jin of mulberry pulp collected from the capital region, Shandong, Henan, and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 德璟力爭，帝留其揭不下，後竟獲免。

translations.literal: Dejing argued forcefully; the Emperor kept his memorial withheld and did not release it; in the end the levy was waived.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing fought the order hard; the Emperor held his memorial back, and in the end the levy was dropped.

sentences.zh: 先以軍儲不足，歲僉畿輔、山東、河南富戶，給值令買米豆輸天津，多至百萬，民大擾。

translations.literal: Earlier, because military stores were insufficient, wealthy households in the capital region, Shandong, and Henan were conscripted each year, paid a price and ordered to buy grain and beans and deliver them to Tianjin—as much as one million piculs—and the people were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, with military stores running short, wealthy households in the capital region, Shandong, and Henan had been drafted each year, paid a set price, and ordered to buy grain and beans for delivery to Tianjin—sometimes as much as a million piculs—and the people were thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 德璟因召對面陳其害，帝即令擬諭罷之。

translations.literal: At audience Dejing stated the harm face to face, and the Emperor immediately ordered a rescript drafted to abolish the practice.
translations.idiomatic: At audience Dejing laid out the harm in person, and the Emperor at once ordered a rescript drafted to abolish the scheme.

sentences.zh: 二月，帝以賊勢漸逼，令群臣會議，以二十二日奏聞。

translations.literal: In the second month, as rebel forces drew gradually nearer, the Emperor ordered the court ministers to confer and report by the twenty-second.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, with rebel armies closing in, the Emperor ordered the ministers to confer and report back by the twenty-second.

sentences.zh: 都御史李邦華密疏雲輔臣知而不敢言。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Li Banghua submitted a secret memorial saying the chief ministers knew but dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Li Banghua sent a secret memorial saying the chief ministers knew the truth but dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 翼日，帝手其疏問何事。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor took the memorial in hand and asked what matter it concerned.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the Emperor took the memorial in hand and asked what it was about.

sentences.zh: 陳演以少詹事項煜東宮南遷議對，帝取視默然。

translations.literal: Chen Yan answered with Junior Grand Mentor Xiang Yu's proposal for the Eastern Palace to move south; the Emperor took it, read it, and fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yan answered with Junior Grand Mentor Xiang Yu's proposal to move the heir apparent south; the Emperor read it and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 德璟從旁力贊，帝不答。

translations.literal: Dejing vigorously endorsed it from the side, but the Emperor did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing pressed the case from the side, but the Emperor gave no answer.

sentences.zh: 給事中光時亨追論練餉之害。

translations.literal: Censor Guang Shiheng pressed the case against the harm of training levies.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guang Shiheng renewed his attack on the harm done by training levies.

sentences.zh: 德璟擬旨：「向來聚斂小人倡為練餉，致民窮禍結，誤國良深。

translations.literal: Dejing drafted the rescript: "Heretofore petty men devoted to extraction advocated training levies, driving the people to destitution and binding calamity upon the realm, deeply injuring the state.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing drafted a rescript: "Petty men bent on extraction invented the training levy, driving the people to ruin and calamity and doing the state grave harm.

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅，詰曰：「聚斂小人誰也？

translations.literal: " The Emperor was displeased and demanded: "Who are these petty extractors?
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor was displeased and demanded, "Who are these petty extractors?

sentences.zh: 」德璟不敢斥嗣昌，以故尚書李待問對。

translations.literal: " Dejing dared not name Sichang; he answered by naming former Minister Li Daiwen.
translations.idiomatic: " Dejing dared not name Sichang outright and answered with the former minister Li Daiwen.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「朕非聚斂，但欲練兵耳。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I am no extractor; I only wished to train troops.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "I am no extractor—I only wanted to train troops.

sentences.zh: 」德璟曰：「陛下豈肯聚斂。

translations.literal: " Dejing said: "Your Majesty would never extract.
translations.idiomatic: " Dejing said, "Your Majesty would never stoop to extraction.

sentences.zh: 然既有舊餉五百萬，新餉九百余萬，復增練餉七百三十萬，臣部實難辭責。

translations.literal: Yet with old provisions already at five million, new provisions at more than nine million, and training levies added at seven million three hundred thousand, my ministry can scarcely escape blame.
translations.idiomatic: Yet with old pay at five million, new pay at more than nine million, and training levies adding another seven million three hundred thousand, my ministry can hardly escape blame.

sentences.zh: 且所練兵馬安在？

translations.literal: Moreover, where are the troops that were trained?
translations.idiomatic: And where are the troops that were supposedly trained?

sentences.zh: 薊督練四萬五千，今止二萬五千。

translations.literal: The Ji supervisor was to train forty-five thousand; today there are only twenty-five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji supervisor was to train forty-five thousand men; today there are only twenty-five thousand.

sentences.zh: 保督練三萬，今止二千五百；

translations.literal: The Bao supervisor was to train thirty thousand; today only two thousand five hundred;
translations.idiomatic: The Baoding supervisor was to train thirty thousand; today there are only two thousand five hundred;

sentences.zh: 保鎮練一萬，今止二百；

translations.literal: Bao garrison was to train ten thousand; today only two hundred;
translations.idiomatic: Baoding garrison was to train ten thousand; today there are only two hundred;

sentences.zh: 若山、永兵七萬八千，薊、密兵十萬，昌平兵四萬，宣大、山西及陜西三邊各二十余萬，一經抽練，原額兵馬俱不問，並所抽亦未練，徒增餉七百余萬，為民累耳。

translations.literal: As for the Shan and Yong forces of seventy-eight thousand, Ji and Mi forces of one hundred thousand, Changping forces of forty thousand, and Xuan-Da, Shanxi, and the three frontiers of Shaanxi each with more than two hundred thousand—once troops were drawn off for training, the original quotas were no longer counted, and even those drawn off were not trained; seven million more in provisions were added for nothing but a burden on the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Shan and Yong armies numbered seventy-eight thousand, Ji and Miyun one hundred thousand, Changping forty thousand, and Xuan-Da, Shanxi, and the three Shaanxi frontiers each more than two hundred thousand—yet once men were skimmed off for training, no one tracked the original rolls, the skimmed troops were never trained, and seven million taels in pay were added for nothing but a burden on the people.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「今已並三餉為一，何必多言！

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "The three levies have now been merged into one—why say more!
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "The three levies are already merged into one—why harp on it!

sentences.zh: 」德璟曰：「戶部雖並為一，州縣追比，仍是三餉。

translations.literal: " Dejing said: "Though the Ministry of Revenue merged them on paper, when prefectures and counties press for payment it is still three levies.
translations.idiomatic: " Dejing said, "The Ministry may have merged them on the books, but when prefectures and counties press for payment it is still three levies.

sentences.zh: 」帝震怒，責以朋比。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was furious and accused him of factional collusion.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor flew into a rage and accused him of factional collusion.

sentences.zh: 德璟力辯，諸輔臣為申救。

translations.literal: Dejing argued forcefully, and the chief ministers interceded on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Dejing defended himself vigorously while the chief ministers pleaded on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 尚書倪元璐以鈔餉乃戶部職，自引咎，帝意稍解。

translations.literal: Minister Ni Yuanlu, holding that paper currency and provisions were the ministry's responsibility, took blame upon himself, and the Emperor's anger eased somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Ni Yuanlu, holding that paper currency and pay were the ministry's charge, took the blame on himself, and the Emperor's anger eased.

sentences.zh: 明日，德璟具疏引罪。

translations.literal: The next day Dejing submitted a full memorial accepting blame.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Dejing submitted a formal memorial accepting blame.

sentences.zh: 帝雖旋罷練餉，而德璟竟以三月二日去位。

translations.literal: Though the Emperor soon abolished the training levy, Dejing nevertheless left office on the second day of the third month.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Emperor soon abolished the training levy, Dejing still left office on the second day of the third month.

sentences.zh: 給事中汪惟效、檢討傅鼎銓等交章乞留，不聽。

translations.literal: Censors Wang Weixiao, Compiler Fu Dingquan, and others submitted memorial after memorial begging he be retained—the Emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Censors Wang Weixiao, Compiler Fu Dingquan, and others sent memorial after memorial begging that he be kept on—the Emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 德璟聞山西陷，未敢行。

translations.literal: Dejing heard that Shanxi had fallen and dared not depart.
translations.idiomatic: When Dejing heard that Shanxi had fallen, he dared not leave the capital.

sentences.zh: 及知廷臣留己，即辭朝，移寓外城。

translations.literal: When he learned that court ministers were keeping him there, he resigned from court session and moved his lodging to the outer city.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the court was keeping him there, he resigned from audience and moved his lodging to the outer city.

sentences.zh: 賊至，得亡去。

translations.literal: When the rebels arrived, he was able to flee.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels arrived, he managed to escape.

sentences.zh: 福王立於南京，召入閣。

translations.literal: The Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing and summoned him into the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Fu was enthroned at Nanjing, he was summoned into the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 自陳三罪，固辭。

translations.literal: He confessed three offenses of his own and firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: He confessed three faults of his own and firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 明年，唐王立於福州，與何吾騶、黃景昉並召。

translations.literal: The next year the Prince of Tang was enthroned at Fuzhou, and he was summoned together with He Wusi and Huang Jingfang.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the Prince of Tang was enthroned at Fuzhou, he was summoned together with He Wusi and Huang Jingfang.

sentences.zh: 又明年以足疾辭歸。

translations.literal: The year after that he resigned and returned home because of a foot ailment.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he resigned and went home, citing a foot ailment.

sentences.zh: 九月，王事敗，而德璟適病篤，遂以是月卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month the princes' cause failed; Dejing happened to be gravely ill and died that same month.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month the princes' cause collapsed; Dejing happened to be gravely ill and died that same month.

sentences.zh: 黃景昉，字太稚，亦晉江人。

translations.literal: Huang Jingfang, courtesy name Taizhi, was also a native of Jinjiang.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Jingfang, courtesy name Taizhi, was also a native of Jinjiang.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of the Tianqi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifth year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士歷官庶子，直日講。

translations.literal: From Hanlin bachelor he rose through posts to Junior Tutor, serving on daily lecture duty.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin bachelor he rose to Junior Tutor and served on daily lecture duty at court.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十一年，帝御經筵，問用人之道。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen, at the classics lecture the Emperor asked about the way of employing men.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year of Chongzhen, at the classics lecture the Emperor asked how men should be chosen for office.

sentences.zh: 景昉言「近日考選不公，推官成勇、朱天麟廉能素著，乃不得預清華選。

translations.literal: Jingfang said, "Recent examination and selection have been unfair. Magistrate-advisors Cheng Yong and Zhu Tianlin have long been known for integrity and ability, yet they were not admitted to elite appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfang said, "Recent examinations have been unfair. Magistrate-advisors Cheng Yong and Zhu Tianlin have long been known for integrity and talent, yet they were passed over for elite appointments.

sentences.zh: 」又言「刑部尚書鄭三俊四朝元老，至清無儔，不當久系獄。

translations.literal: " He also said, "Minister of Justice Zheng Sanjun, a veteran of four reigns, unmatched in probity, ought not remain long imprisoned.
translations.idiomatic: " He also said, "Minister of Justice Zheng Sanjun, a veteran of four reigns and unmatched in probity, ought not languish in prison.

sentences.zh: 」退復上章論之，三俊旋獲釋，勇等亦俱改官。

translations.literal: " After retiring he again submitted a memorial on the matter; Sanjun was soon released, and Yong and the others were all given new posts.
translations.idiomatic: " After leaving court he submitted another memorial on the matter; Sanjun was soon released, and Yong and the others were all given new posts.

sentences.zh: 景昉尋進少詹事。

translations.literal: Jingfang was soon promoted to Junior Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfang was soon promoted to Junior Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 嘗召對，言：「近撤還監視中官高起潛，關外輒聞警報，疑此中有隱情。

translations.literal: On one occasion at audience he said: "Recently the supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian was recalled from the frontier; immediately alarms sounded outside the passes—I suspect hidden motives behind this.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion at audience he said, "The supervising eunuch Gao Qiqian was recently recalled from the frontier, and alarms at once sounded beyond the passes—I suspect something hidden behind this.

sentences.zh: 臣家海濱，見沿海將吏每遇調發，即報海警，冀得復留。

translations.literal: My family lives on the coast; I have seen that whenever coastal officers and officials face transfer, they report a naval alarm, hoping to be kept in place.
translations.idiomatic: My family lives on the coast; I have seen coastal officers report a naval alarm whenever transfer orders arrive, hoping to be kept in place.

sentences.zh: 觸類而推，其情自見。

translations.literal: Draw the analogy and the truth becomes plain.
translations.idiomatic: Draw the parallel and the motive becomes plain.

sentences.zh: 」帝頷之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor nodded assent.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 十四年以詹事兼掌翰林院。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he served as Grand Mentor while also heading the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he served as Grand Mentor while also heading the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 時庶常停選已久，景昉具疏請復，又請召還修撰劉同升、編修趙士春，皆不報。

translations.literal: Hanlin probationary appointments had long been suspended; Jingfang submitted a detailed memorial asking they be restored, and also asked that Compiler Liu Tongsheng and Editor Zhao Shichun be recalled—all without response.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin probationary appointments had long been suspended; Jingfang submitted a detailed memorial asking that they be restored, and also asked that Compiler Liu Tongsheng and Editor Zhao Shichun be recalled—none of it received a reply.

sentences.zh: 十五年六月召對稱旨，與蔣德璟、吳甡並相。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year, pleasing the Emperor at audience, he was made Grand Secretary together with Jiang Dejing and Wu Shen.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year he pleased the Emperor at audience and was made Grand Secretary together with Jiang Dejing and Wu Shen.

sentences.zh: 明年並加太子少保，改戶部尚書、文淵閣。

translations.literal: The next year all were additionally made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and the Wenyuan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The next year all three were made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent; he was transferred to Minister of Revenue and the Wenyuan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 南京操江故設文武二員，帝欲裁去文臣，專任誠意伯劉孔昭。

translations.literal: For Nanjing river defense there had long been both civil and military commissioners; the Emperor wished to cut the civil post and put all authority in the hands of the Earl of Chengyi, Liu Kongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Nanjing river defense had long been entrusted to both a civil and a military commissioner; the Emperor wished to abolish the civil post and give sole charge to the Earl of Chengyi, Liu Kongzhao.

sentences.zh: 副都御史惠世揚遲久不至，帝命削其籍。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Hui Shiyang was long overdue and had not arrived; the Emperor ordered his name struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Censor-in-Chief Hui Shiyang was long overdue and had not reported; the Emperor ordered his name struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 景昉俱揭爭，帝不悅，遂連疏引歸。

translations.literal: Jingfang memorialized against both measures; the Emperor was displeased, and he submitted successive memorials requesting retirement.
translations.idiomatic: Jingfang memorialized against both decisions; the Emperor was displeased, and he sent successive memorials asking to retire.

sentences.zh: 唐王時，召入直，未幾，復告歸。

translations.literal: Under the Prince of Tang he was summoned to serve at court; before long he again asked leave to return home.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Prince of Tang he was summoned back to court; before long he again asked leave to go home.

sentences.zh: 國變後，家居十數年始卒。

translations.literal: After the dynastic catastrophe he lived at home more than ten years before he died.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the dynasty he lived at home for more than ten years before he died.

sentences.zh: 方岳貢，字四長，谷城人。

translations.literal: Fang Yuegong, courtesy name Sichang, was a native of Gucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Yuegong, courtesy name Sichang, was a native of Gucheng.

sentences.zh: 天啟二年進士。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of the Tianqi reign.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the second year of Tianqi.

sentences.zh: 授戶部主事，進郎中。

translations.literal: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and advanced to director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Revenue and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 歷典倉庫，督永平糧儲，並以廉謹聞。

translations.literal: He successively managed the granaries, supervised Yongping grain reserves, and in both roles was known for integrity and diligence.
translations.idiomatic: He successively managed the granaries and supervised Yongping grain reserves, earning a reputation in both posts for integrity and diligence.

sentences.zh: 崇禎元年，出為松江知府。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chongzhen he went out to serve as prefect of Songjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chongzhen he was sent out as prefect of Songjiang.

sentences.zh: 海濱多盜，捕得輒杖殺之。

translations.literal: Pirates were numerous along the coast; when captured they were beaten to death on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Pirates were rife along the coast; when captured they were beaten to death on the spot.

sentences.zh: 郡東南臨大海，颶潮沖擊，時為民患，築石堤二十里許，遂為永利。

translations.literal: The prefecture's southeast faced the sea; hurricane tides battered the shore and often harmed the people; he built a stone dike some twenty li long, turning flood into lasting benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture's southeast faced the sea, and hurricane tides battered the shore to the people's ruin; he built a stone dike some twenty li long and turned the flood into lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 郡漕京師數十萬石，而諸倉乃相距五里，為築城垣護之，名曰「倉城」。

translations.literal: The prefecture shipped several hundred thousand shi of tribute grain to the capital, yet the granaries stood five li apart; he built city walls to protect them, calling the place "Granary City."
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture shipped several hundred thousand shi of tribute grain to the capital, yet its granaries stood five li apart; he built walls to protect them and called the place Granary City.

sentences.zh: 他救荒助役、修學課士，鹹有成績，舉卓異者數矣。

translations.literal: In relief work, public labor, rebuilding schools, and examining scholars, he likewise achieved results and was several times recommended for outstanding service.
translations.idiomatic: In famine relief, public labor, rebuilding schools, and examining scholars he likewise achieved results and was several times recommended for outstanding service.

sentences.zh: 薛國觀敗，其私人上海王陛彥下吏，素有隙，因言岳貢嘗饋國觀三千金，遂被逮。

translations.literal: When Xue Guoguan fell, his client Wang Shiyan of Shanghai was arrested; having long borne a grudge, Shiyan claimed Yuegong had once given Guoguan three thousand taels of gold, and Yuegong was thereupon arrested.
translations.idiomatic: When Xue Guoguan fell, his client Wang Shiyan of Shanghai was arrested; having long borne a grudge, Shiyan claimed Yuegong had once given Guoguan three thousand taels of gold, and Yuegong was arrested.

sentences.zh: 士民詣闕訟冤，巡撫黃希亦白其誣，下法司讞奏。

translations.literal: Gentry and common people went to the palace gates to plead his innocence; Governor Huang Xi also reported that the charge was false, and the case was sent to the legal offices for judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry and commoners went to the palace gates to plead his innocence; Governor Huang Xi also reported that the charge was false, and the case was sent to the legal offices for judgment.

sentences.zh: 一日，帝晏見輔臣，問：「有一知府積俸十余年，屢舉卓異者誰也？

translations.literal: One day at an informal evening audience with the chief ministers the Emperor asked: "Which prefect has accumulated salary for more than ten years and been repeatedly recommended for outstanding service?
translations.idiomatic: One day at an informal evening audience the Emperor asked the chief ministers, "Which prefect has served more than ten years on accumulated salary and been repeatedly recommended for outstanding service?

sentences.zh: 」蔣德璟以岳貢對。

translations.literal: " Dejing answered with Yuegong.
translations.idiomatic: " Dejing answered with Yuegong.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「今安在？

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "Where is he now?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Where is he now?

sentences.zh: 」德璟復以陛彥株連對，帝頷之。

translations.literal: " Dejing again answered that he was implicated through Shiyan; the Emperor nodded.
translations.idiomatic: " Dejing answered that he had been implicated through Shiyan; the Emperor nodded.

sentences.zh: 法司讞上，言行賄無實跡，宜復官。

translations.literal: The legal offices reported their finding: there was no solid evidence of bribery, and his office should be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The legal offices reported that there was no solid evidence of bribery and that his office should be restored.

sentences.zh: 帝獎其清執，報可。

translations.literal: The Emperor praised his incorruptible conduct and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor praised his incorruptible conduct and approved.

sentences.zh: 無何，給事中方士亮薦岳貢及蘇州知府陳洪謐，乃擢山東副使兼右參議，總理江南糧儲。

translations.literal: Before long Censor Fang Shiliang recommended Yuegong and Chen Hongmi, prefect of Suzhou; Yuegong was then promoted to Vice Commissioner of Shandong while also serving as Right Assistant Commissioner, with general supervision of Jiangnan grain reserves.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Censor Fang Shiliang recommended Yuegong and Chen Hongmi, prefect of Suzhou; Yuegong was promoted to Vice Commissioner of Shandong while also serving as Right Assistant Commissioner, with general charge of Jiangnan grain reserves.

sentences.zh: 所督漕艘，如期抵通州。

translations.literal: The grain barges he supervised reached Tongzhou on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: The grain barges under his supervision reached Tongzhou on schedule.

sentences.zh: 帝大喜。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書鄭三俊舉天下廉能監司五人，岳貢與焉。

translations.literal: Minister of Personnel Zheng Sanjun nominated five incorruptible and capable surveillance commissioners under Heaven, and Yuegong was among them.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Personnel Zheng Sanjun nominated five incorruptible and capable surveillance commissioners from across the realm, and Yuegong was among them.

sentences.zh: 帝趣使入對，見於平臺，問為政何先，對曰：「欲天下治平，在擇守令；

translations.literal: The Emperor urgently summoned him for audience, received him at the Ping Platform, and asked what should come first in governing; he answered: "If one wishes the realm brought to order and peace, the key lies in choosing prefects and magistrates;
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor urgently summoned him for audience, received him at the Ping Platform, and asked what should come first in governing; he answered, "If the realm is to be brought to order and peace, the first thing is choosing prefects and magistrates;

sentences.zh: 察守令賢否，在監司；

translations.literal: to discern whether prefects and magistrates are worthy lies with the surveillance commissioners;
translations.idiomatic: to judge whether prefects and magistrates are worthy lies with the surveillance commissioners;

sentences.zh: 察監司賢否，在巡方；

translations.literal: to discern whether surveillance commissioners are worthy lies with the touring inspectors;
translations.idiomatic: to judge whether surveillance commissioners are worthy lies with the touring inspectors;

sentences.zh: 察巡方賢否，在總憲。

translations.literal: to discern whether touring inspectors are worthy lies with the censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: to judge whether touring inspectors are worthy lies with the censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 總憲得人，御史安敢以身試法。

translations.literal: If the chief surveillance commissioner is the right man, how would a censor dare test the law with his own person?
translations.idiomatic: With the right chief surveillance commissioner in place, no censor would dare flout the law.

sentences.zh: 」帝善之，賜食，日晡乃出。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved, granted him a meal, and only let him leave in the late afternoon.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was pleased, gave him a meal, and did not let him leave until late afternoon.

sentences.zh: 越六日，即超擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: Six days later he was abruptly promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Six days later he was abruptly promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 嘗召對，帝適以事詰吏部尚書李遇知。

translations.literal: Once when summoned to audience, the emperor happened to be questioning Minister of Personnel Li Yuzhi about a matter.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion when summoned to audience, the emperor happened to be questioning Minister of Personnel Li Yuzhi about a matter.

sentences.zh: 遇知曰：「臣正糾駁。

translations.literal: Yuzhi said: "Your servant is just now impeaching and rebutting.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi said, "I am in the midst of impeaching and rebutting the case.

sentences.zh: 」岳貢曰：「何不即題參？

translations.literal: " Yuegong said: "Why not memorialize at once?
translations.idiomatic: " Yuegong said, "Why not submit a memorial at once?

sentences.zh: 」深合帝意。

translations.literal: " This deeply accorded with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: " This struck the emperor as exactly right.

sentences.zh: 翼日，命以本官兼東閣大學士，時十六年十一月也。

translations.literal: The next day he was ordered to serve in his present office concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion—it was the eleventh month of the sixteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he was ordered to keep his present office while also serving as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion—it was the eleventh month of the sixteenth year.

sentences.zh: 故事，閣臣無帶都御史銜者，自岳貢始。

translations.literal: By precedent no grand secretary had borne the censor-in-chief title; this began with Yuegong.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent no grand secretary had held the censor-in-chief title; Yuegong was the first.

sentences.zh: 岳貢本吏材。

translations.literal: Yuegong was by nature a man of administrative talent.
translations.idiomatic: Yuegong was by nature a man of administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 及為相，務勾檢簿書，請核赦前舊賦，意主搜括，聲名甚損。

translations.literal: When he became chief minister he devoted himself to auditing ledgers, requested verification of old levies before amnesty, and aimed chiefly at exaction—his reputation suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Once he became chief minister he devoted himself to auditing ledgers and called for verification of old levies antedating amnesty, aiming chiefly at exaction—and his reputation suffered greatly.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月命以戶、兵二部尚書兼文淵閣大學士總督漕運、屯田、練兵諸務，駐濟寧。

translations.literal: In the second month of the seventeenth year he was ordered to serve as Minister of Revenue and Minister of War concurrently with Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth, directing grain transport, military colonies, troop training, and other affairs, stationed at Jining.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the seventeenth year he was ordered to serve as Minister of Revenue and Minister of War while also Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Depth, directing grain transport, military colonies, troop training, and other affairs from Jining.

sentences.zh: 已而不行。

translations.literal: Before long the order was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the arrangement was not carried out.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷京師，岳貢及邱瑜被執，幽劉宗敏所。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took the capital, Yuegong and Qiu Yu were seized and confined in Liu Zongmin's quarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng took the capital, Yuegong and Qiu Yu were seized and held in Liu Zongmin's quarters.

sentences.zh: 賊索銀，岳貢素廉，貧無以應，拷掠備至。

translations.literal: The rebels demanded silver; Yuegong had always been incorrupt and was too poor to comply, and torture was applied to the full.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels demanded silver; Yuegong had always been incorrupt and was too poor to pay, and he was tortured without mercy.

sentences.zh: 搜其邸，無所有，松江賈人為代輸千金。

translations.literal: They searched his residence and found nothing; a merchant from Songjiang paid a thousand taels on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: They searched his residence and found nothing; a merchant from Songjiang paid a thousand taels on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 四月朔日與瑜並釋。

translations.literal: On the first day of the fourth month he and Qiu were released together.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the fourth month he and Qiu were released together.

sentences.zh: 十二日，賊既殺陳演等，令監守者並殺二人，監守者奉以繯，二人並縊死。

translations.literal: On the twelfth day, after the rebels had killed Chen Yan and others, they ordered the guards to kill the two men as well; the guards offered them cords, and both were strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: On the twelfth day, after the rebels had killed Chen Yan and others, they ordered the guards to kill the two men as well; the guards offered them cords, and both hanged themselves.

sentences.zh: 邱瑜，宜城人。

translations.literal: Qiu Yu was a man of Yicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Yu came from Yicheng.

sentences.zh: 天啟五年進士。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianqi he became a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of the Tianqi reign.

sentences.zh: 由庶吉士授檢討。

translations.literal: From bachelor he was appointed reviser.
translations.idiomatic: From Hanlin bachelor he was appointed reviser.

sentences.zh: 崇禎中，屢遷少詹事。

translations.literal: In the Chongzhen reign he was repeatedly promoted to Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chongzhen he rose repeatedly to Junior Commissioner of the Household for the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 襄陽陷，瑜上恤難宗、擇才吏、旌死節、停催征、蘇郵困、禁勞役六事。

translations.literal: When Xiangyang fell, Qiu memorialized six measures: succor for the imperial clan in distress, selection of talented officials, commendation of those who died loyal, halting urgent levies, relief for postal distress, and prohibition of corvée labor.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiangyang fell, Qiu memorialized six measures: succor for the imperial clan in distress, selection of talented officials, commendation of those who died loyal, halting urgent levies, relief for postal distress, and prohibition of corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 帝采納焉。

translations.literal: The emperor adopted them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor adopted them.

sentences.zh: 歷禮部左右侍郎。

translations.literal: He rose through the Left and Right Vice Minister posts of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the Left and Right Vice Minister posts of Rites.

sentences.zh: 因召對，言：「督師孫傳庭出關，安危所系，慎勿促之輕出。

translations.literal: When summoned to audience he said: "Grand Coordinator Sun Chuanting's sortie beyond the passes bears on safety and peril—take care not to urge him to move out lightly.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to audience he said, "Grand Coordinator Sun Chuanting's sortie beyond the passes bears on the fate of the realm—take care not to urge him to march out lightly.

sentences.zh: 俾鎮定關中，猶可號召諸將，相機進剿。

translations.literal: Let him steady Guanzhong; he can still rally the generals and advance to suppress the enemy as opportunity allows."
translations.idiomatic: Let him steady Guanzhong; he can still rally the generals and advance to suppress the enemy when the moment is right."

sentences.zh: 」帝不能從。

translations.literal: The emperor could not follow this advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would not follow this advice.

sentences.zh: 十七年正月以本官兼東閣大學士，同範景文入閣。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventeenth year he was ordered to serve in his present office concurrently as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the Grand Secretariat together with Fan Jingwen.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the seventeenth year he was ordered to keep his present office while also serving as Grand Secretary of the Eastern Pavilion, entering the Grand Secretariat together with Fan Jingwen.

sentences.zh: 都城陷，受拷掠者再，搜獲止二千金，既而被害。

translations.literal: When the capital fell he was tortured twice; only two thousand taels were found in the search, and afterward he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell he was tortured twice; only two thousand taels were found in the search, and afterward he was killed.

sentences.zh: 瑜子之陶，年少有幹略。

translations.literal: Qiu's son Zhizhi was young but capable and resourceful.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu's son Zhizhi was young but capable and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 李自成陷宜城，瑜父民忠罵賊而死。

translations.literal: When Li Zicheng took Yicheng, Qiu's father Minzhong cursed the rebels and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zicheng took Yicheng, Qiu's father Minzhong cursed the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 之陶被獲，用為兵政府從事，尋以本府侍郎守襄陽。

translations.literal: Zhizhi was captured and employed as an aide in the military government; soon he was made vice minister of that government to guard Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi was captured and employed as an aide in the military government; soon he was made vice minister of that government to guard Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 襄陽尹牛佺，賊相金星子，其倚任不如也。

translations.literal: Niu Quan, magistrate of Xiangyang, was the son of the rebel minister Venus; his reliance on him was not equal to that on Zhizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Niu Quan, magistrate of Xiangyang, was the son of the rebel minister Venus; Li relied on him less than on Zhizhi.

sentences.zh: 之陶以蠟丸書貽傳庭曰：「督師與之戰，吾詭言左鎮兵大至，搖其心，彼必返顧。

translations.literal: Zhizhi sent Sun Chuanting a letter in a wax pellet, saying: "When the grand coordinator fights him, I will falsely report that the Left Garrison's troops have arrived in force to shake their hearts—they are sure to look back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi sent Sun Chuanting a letter in a wax pellet, saying, "When you fight him, I will falsely report that the Left Garrison's troops have arrived in force to shake their hearts—they are sure to look back.

sentences.zh: 督師擊其後，吾從中起，賊可滅也。

translations.literal: The grand coordinator strikes from the rear, I rise in the middle—the rebels can be destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: You strike from the rear, I rise in the middle—and the rebels can be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 」傳庭大喜，報書如其言，為賊邏者所得。

translations.literal: " Chuanting was greatly pleased and replied as proposed; the letter was captured by rebel scouts.
translations.idiomatic: " Chuanting was greatly pleased and replied as proposed; the letter was captured by rebel scouts.

sentences.zh: 傳庭恃內應，連營前進，之陶果舉火，報左兵大至。

translations.literal: Chuanting relied on the inside contact and advanced camp after camp; Zhizhi indeed raised signal fires, reporting that the Left Garrison's troops had arrived in force.
translations.idiomatic: Chuanting relied on the inside contact and advanced camp after camp; Zhizhi indeed raised signal fires, reporting that the Left Garrison's troops had arrived in force.

sentences.zh: 自成驗得其詐，召而示以傳庭書，責其負己。

translations.literal: Zicheng verified the deception, summoned him, showed him Chuanting's letter, and reproached him for betraying him.
translations.idiomatic: Zicheng verified the deception, summoned him, showed him Chuanting's letter, and reproached him for betraying him.

sentences.zh: 之陶大罵曰：「吾恨不斬汝萬段，豈從汝反耶！

translations.literal: Zhizhi cursed loudly: "I regret I could not cut you into ten thousand pieces—how would I follow you in rebellion!
translations.idiomatic: Zhizhi cursed loudly, "I regret I could not cut you into ten thousand pieces—how would I follow you in rebellion!

sentences.zh: 」賊怒，支解之。

translations.literal: " The rebels were enraged and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels were enraged and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：莊烈帝在位僅十七年，輔相至五十余人。

translations.literal: The commentator says: The Chongzhen Emperor reigned only seventeen years, yet chief ministers numbered more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: The Chongzhen Emperor reigned only seventeen years, yet chief ministers numbered more than fifty.

sentences.zh: 其克保令名者，數人而已，若標等是也。

translations.literal: Those who could preserve a good name were only a few, such as Biao and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Those who could preserve a good name were only a few—men such as Biao.

sentences.zh: 基命能推轂舊輔以定危難，震孟以風節顯，德璟諳悉舊章。

translations.literal: Jiming could promote old chief ministers to settle crisis; Zhenmeng was distinguished by integrity; Dejing was thoroughly versed in old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Jiming could promote old chief ministers to settle crisis; Zhenmeng was distinguished by integrity; Dejing was thoroughly versed in old regulations.

sentences.zh: 以陸喜之論薛瑩者觀之，所謂侃然體國，執正不懼，斟酌時宜，時獻微益者乎。

translations.literal: Viewed by the standard of Lu Xi's judgment on Xue Ying, they were what is called men who uprightly embodied the state, held to right without fear, weighed the times, and from time to time offered small benefits.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by the standard of Lu Xi's praise of Xue Ying, they were men who uprightly embodied the state, held to right without fear, weighed the times, and from time to time offered modest benefits.

sentences.zh: 至於扶危定傾，殆非易言也。

translations.literal: As for supporting a tottering state and setting it upright, that was hardly easy to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: As for supporting a tottering state and setting it upright, that was another matter entirely.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，國步方艱，人材亦與俱盡，其所由來者漸矣。

translations.literal: Alas—the nation's step was already hard, and talent was exhausted along with it; the causes had long been gathering.
translations.idiomatic: Alas—the realm was already in peril, and talent was exhausted along with it; the causes had long been gathering.
